body.text: Haribhadrasūrikṛtā Nyāyapraveśapravṛttiḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Nyāyapraveśapravṛtti</s> (Exposition of the Introduction to Logic), composed by <s>Haribhadrasūri</s>.

body.text: śrīsarvajñāya namaḥ //
body.translated_text: Homage to the glorious Omniscient One!

children.translated_text: Having bowed to <s>Jineśvara</s> (the Lord of Conquerors), the expounder of right knowledge,
I compose a commentary on the <s>Nyāyapraveśa</s> (Introduction to Logic) with clear meaning.
Although it has been composed by the learned, both in detail and in brief,
[I], though of poor understanding, with a taste for conciseness, [compose this] out of compassion for beings.
<s>Sādhana</s> (proof) and <s>dūṣaṇa</s> (refutation), together with their semblances, are for communicating to others (<s>parasaṃvid</s>);
<s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference), together with their semblances, are for self-cognition (<s>ātmasaṃvid</s>).

body.text: ityādāveva ślokaḥ / āhāsya kimādāvupanyāsa iti / ucyate / iha prekṣāpūrvakāriṇaḥ prayojanādiśūnye na kvacitpravartanta ityato 'dhikṛtaśāstrasya prayojanādipradarśanena prekṣāvatāṃ pravṛttyarthamiti / śāstrārthakathanakālopasthitaparasaṃbhāvyamānānupanyāsahetunirākaraṇārthaṃ ca nyāyapraveśakākhyaṃ śāstramārabhyate ityukte saṃbhavatyevaṃvādī paraḥ- nārabdhavyamidaṃ prayojanarahitatvāt unmattakavākyavat / tathā nirabhidheyatvāt kākadantaparīkṣāvat / tathā asaṃbaddhatvāt daśa dāḍimāni ṣaḍapūpāḥ kuṇḍamajājinaṃ palalapiṇḍaṃ sara kīṭiketyādivākyavat / tadamīṣāṃ hetūnāmasiddhatodbhāvayiṣayā prayojanādipratipādanārthamādau ślokopanyāsa / ayaṃ cābhidheyaprayojane eva darśayati sākṣāt saṃbandhaṃ tu sāmarthyena / yathā caitadevaṃ tathā sukhapratipattyarthamevameva leśato vyākhyāya darśayiṣyāmaḥ // vyākhyā ca padavākyasaṃgateti / uktaṃ ca-
body.translated_text: This verse appears at the very beginning. One asks: What is the purpose of presenting it at the outset? It is said: Here, those who act with deliberation do not engage in anything devoid of purpose and so forth; therefore, by showing the purpose and other [features] of the treatise under discussion, [this is done] in order to motivate the engagement of the discerning. And in order to remove the reasons that an opponent might conceive at the time when the content of the treatise is about to be stated, the treatise called <s>Nyāyapraveśa</s> is commenced. When this is said, an opponent may speak thus: 'This should not be commenced, because it lacks purpose — like the speech of a madman. Likewise, because it has no subject-matter — like examining the teeth of a crow. Likewise, because it lacks coherence — like the statement: ten pomegranates, six cakes, a pot, a goat-skin, a lump of straw, a lake, an insect,' and so on. Therefore, intending to demonstrate the unestablished nature of these reasons, a verse is presented at the outset to set forth the purpose and the like. And this [verse] directly shows the subject-matter and purpose, and the connection indirectly through implication. That this is so, we shall demonstrate by explaining it briefly for ease of understanding. And the commentary is of the type that proceeds through word and sentence. And it has been said —

children.translated_text: How can the true meaning of treatises, chapters, and the like be understood

children.text: vyākhyāṃ vihāya tattvajñaiḥ sā coktā padavākyayoḥ //
children.translated_text: without a commentary? And that [commentary], say the knowers of truth, is of words and sentences.

body.text: tatrāpi padasamudāyātmakatvādvākyasyādau padārthagamanikā nyāyyā /
body.translated_text: Moreover, since a sentence is constituted by an aggregate of words, it is proper to first ascertain the meanings of words.

body.text: sā ca padavibhāgapūrvetyataḥ padavibhāgaḥ /
body.translated_text: And since that [word-meaning analysis] is preceded by word-division, [we give] the word-division:

body.text: sādhanam dūṣaṇam ca eva sābhāsam parasaṃvide pratyakṣam anumānam ca sābhāsam tu ātmasaṃvide iti padāni //
body.translated_text: The words are: <s>sādhanam</s> (proof), <s>dūṣaṇam</s> (refutation), <s>ca</s> (and), <s>eva</s> (only), <s>sābhāsam</s> (together with semblances), <s>parasaṃvide</s> (for communicating to others), <s>pratyakṣam</s> (perception), <s>anumānam</s> (inference), <s>ca</s> (and), <s>sābhāsam</s> (together with semblances), <s>tu</s> (but), <s>ātmasaṃvide</s> (for self-cognition).

body.text: adhunā padārtha ucyate / sādhyate aneneti siddhirvā sādhayatīti vā sādhanam / tacca pakṣādivacanajātam / vakṣyati ca / pakṣādivacanāni sādhanam / viṣayaścāsya dharmaviśiṣṭo dharmī /
body.translated_text: Now the word-meanings are stated. <s>Sādhana</s> (proof): 'That by which [something] is established' — thus it is [either] establishment (<s>siddhi</s>), or 'it establishes' — thus it is the means of proof. And this is the set of statements consisting of the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) and the rest. And it will be stated: 'The statements of the thesis and the rest constitute the proof.' And its object is the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>) qualified by a property.

body.text: tathā dūṣyate 'nena dūṣayatīti vā dūṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: Likewise, <s>dūṣaṇa</s> (refutation): 'That by which [something] is refuted' or 'it refutes' — thus it is refutation.

body.text: tacca sādhanadoṣodbhāvanaṃ vacanajātameva /
body.translated_text: And this is the set of statements that expose the faults of a proof.

body.text: vakṣyati ca sādhanadoṣodbhāvanāni dūṣaṇāni / viṣayaścāsya sādhanābhāsaḥ na samyaksādhanam / tasya duṣayitumaśakyatvāt /
body.translated_text: And it will be stated: 'Expositions of the faults of a proof are refutations.' And its object is a semblance of proof (<s>sādhanābhāsa</s>), not a valid proof, since that [valid proof] cannot be refuted.

body.text: nanu vakṣyati sādhanadoṣodbhāvanāni dūṣaṇānīti tadetatkatham / ucyate /
body.translated_text: Now, an objection: It will be stated that 'expositions of the faults of a proof are refutations' — how then [is this consistent]? It is said:

body.text: sādhanābhāsa eva kiṃcitsāmyena sādhanopacārādadoṣaḥ ityetacca tatraiva nirloṭhayiṣyāmaḥ / caśabdaḥ samuccaye / evakāro 'vadhāraṇe / sa cānyayogavyavacchedārtha ityetaddarśayiṣyāmaḥ / tathā ābhāsanamābhāsaḥ / saha ābhāsena vartate sābhāsam / sābhāsaśabdaḥ pratyekamabhisaṃbadhyate /
body.translated_text: A semblance of proof, by virtue of a certain similarity, is figuratively called 'proof' — and this is not a fault. This too we shall thoroughly examine in that [relevant] place. The word <s>ca</s> is for conjunction. The word <s>eva</s> is for restriction. And that [restriction] is for the purpose of excluding other connections — this we shall demonstrate. Likewise, <s>ābhāsa</s> (semblance) is 'shining forth' (appearance); that which occurs together with a semblance is <s>sābhāsa</s>. The word <s>sābhāsa</s> connects with each individually.

body.text: sādhanaṃ sābhāsaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ sābhāsam / tatra sādhanābhāsaṃ pakṣābhāsādi / vakṣyati ca / sādhayitumiṣṭo 'pi pratyakṣādiviruddhaḥ pakṣābhāsa ityādi / dūṣaṇābhāsaṃ cābhūtasādhanadoṣodbhāvanāni /
body.translated_text: 'Proof together with its semblance' and 'refutation together with its semblance.' Therein, a semblance of proof is a semblance of the thesis and so on. And it will be stated: 'A thesis-semblance is that which, though desired to be established, is contradicted by perception and the like,' and so forth. And a semblance of refutation is the exposition of non-existent faults of a proof.

body.text: vakṣyati ca abhūtasādhanadoṣodbhāvanāni dūṣaṇābhāsānīti // parasaṃvide ityatra pare prāśnikāḥ saṃvedanaṃ saṃvid avabodha ityarthaḥ / pareṣāṃ saṃvit parasaṃvit tasyai parasaṃvide parāvabodhāya / iyaṃ tādarthye caturthī / yathā yūpāya dāruḥ / iti padārthaḥ // vākyarthastvayam / sādhanadūṣaṇe eva sābhāse parasaṃvide parāvabodhāya na pratyakṣānumāne /
body.translated_text: And it will be stated: 'Expositions of non-existent faults of a proof are semblances of refutation.' Regarding <s>parasaṃvide</s>: 'others' (<s>para</s>) means the questioners; <s>saṃvedana</s> is <s>saṃvid</s>, meaning 'understanding.' The understanding of others is <s>parasaṃvid</s>; for that [understanding], [it is] <s>parasaṃvide</s>, meaning 'for the understanding of others.' This is the dative of purpose, as in 'wood for a sacrificial post.' Thus [ends] the word-meaning. But the sentence-meaning is this: proof and refutation alone, together with their semblances, are for the understanding of others — not perception and inference.

body.text: parasaṃvitphalatvāttayoḥ / yathā pārtha eva dhanurdharaḥ pārthe dhanurdhārayati sati ko 'nyo dhanurdhārayati iti // pratyakṣam ityatra akṣamindriyaṃ tataśca pratigatamakṣaṃ pratyakṣaṃ kāryatvenendriyaṃ prati gatamityarthaḥ / idaṃ ca vakṣyati pratyakṣaṃ kalpanāpoḍham ityādi / tathā mīyate aneneti mānaṃ paricchedyata ityarthaḥ / anuśabdaḥ paścādarthe / paścānmānaṃ anumānam /
body.translated_text: because those two [i.e., proof and refutation] have as their result the cognition of another (<s>parasaṃvit</s>). Just as [in the example:] '<s>Pārtha</s> alone is the archer' — when <s>Pārtha</s> holds the bow, who else holds it? Regarding the word '<s>pratyakṣa</s>' (perception): '<s>akṣa</s>' means the sense-organ (<s>indriya</s>); and '<s>pratyakṣa</s>' means 'directed toward the sense-organ' — the meaning is: [that cognition which] has reached the sense-organ by way of being its effect. This will be stated [later]: '<s>Pratyakṣa</s> (perception) is that which is free from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>)' and so forth. Likewise, '<s>māna</s>' (measure/means of knowledge): that by which something is measured — the meaning is: that by which [an object] is ascertained. The prefix '<s>anu</s>' has the sense of 'after'; 'measure after' [i.e., subsequent measurement] is <s>anumāna</s> (inference),

body.text: pakṣadharmagrahaṇasaṃbandhasmaraṇapūrvakamityarthaḥ / vakṣyati ca trirūpālliṅgālliṅgini jñānamanumānam / caśabdaḥ pūrvavat / sābhāsam ityādi / vakṣyati ca kalpanājñānamarthāntare pratyakṣābhāsam ityādi / tathā hetvābhāsapūrvakaṃ jñānamanumānābhāsam ityādi ca / tu śabdastvevakārārthaḥ / sa cāvadhāraṇa iti darśayiṣyāmaḥ // ātmasaṃvide iti / atatītyātmā jīvaḥ / saṃvedanaṃ saṃvit / ātmanaḥ saṃvit ātmasaṃvit / tasyai ātmasaṃvide ātmāvabodhāya / ātmā ceha cittacaittasaṃtānarūpaḥ parigṛhyate na tu paraparikalpito nittyatvādidharmā /
body.translated_text: meaning: [a cognition that is] preceded by the apprehension of the property of the subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) and the recollection of the relation. And it will be stated: 'The knowledge of the <s>liṅgin</s> (the property-possessor) from the <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark) possessing three characteristics is <s>anumāna</s> (inference).' The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) is [used] as before. '[Together] with their semblances (<s>sābhāsa</s>)' and so forth — it will be stated: 'Conceptual cognition is the semblance of perception (<s>pratyakṣābhāsa</s>) with respect to another object' and so forth. Likewise: 'Cognition preceded by a pseudo-reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) is the semblance of inference (<s>anumānābhāsa</s>)' and so forth. The word '<s>tu</s>' has the meaning of '<s>eva</s>' (only/exclusively). And we shall show that it has the force of restriction (<s>avadhāraṇa</s>). Regarding '<s>ātmasaṃvide</s>': '<s>ātmā</s>' — that which goes — [means] the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul); '<s>saṃvit</s>' — cognition; '<s>ātmasaṃvit</s>' — cognition of the self; 'for the sake of <s>ātmasaṃvit</s>' — for self-understanding. And here '<s>ātman</s>' is accepted as being of the nature of the continuum of mind and mental factors (<s>cittacaittasaṃtāna</s>), not [the <s>ātman</s>] endowed with attributes like permanence as imagined by others,

body.text: tatpratipādakapramāṇābhāvāt / iti padārthaḥ // vākyārthastvayam / pratyakṣānumāne eva sābhāse ātmasaṃvide ātmāvabodhāya na sādhanadūṣaṇe ātmasaṃvitphalatvāt tayoḥ / āha nanu sādhanamapi vastuto 'numānameva tataścānumānamityādyukte sādhanābhidhānaṃ na yujyate asminvā prāgukte anumānābhidhānamiti / naiṣa doṣaḥ / svārthaparārthabhedanābhidhānāt / tatra sādhanaṃ parārthamanumānamidaṃ punaḥ svārtham / aparastvāha / ādau sādhanadūṣaṇābhidhānamayuktaṃ pratyakṣānumānapuraḥsarattvāttatprayogasya / ucyate / satyapi tatpuraḥsaratve śāstrārambhasya parasaṃvitpradhānatvātsādhanadūṣaṇayorapi tatphalatvātpratyāsatterādāvupanyāsaḥ / parārthanibandhanaḥ svārtha iti nyāyapradarśanārthamanye //
body.translated_text: because there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) establishing that [permanent <s>ātman</s>]. This is the meaning of the words. The meaning of the sentence is as follows: Perception and inference alone, together with their semblances, serve for self-understanding (<s>ātmasaṃvit</s>) — not proof and refutation — because those two [perception and inference] have self-cognition as their result. One might object: 'Proof (<s>sādhana</s>) is in reality nothing but inference; therefore, since inference has already been mentioned, the mention of proof is not appropriate — or alternatively, given the prior mention [of proof], the mention of inference [is redundant].' This is no fault, because there is [a separate] mention due to the distinction between [inference] for one's own sake (<s>svārtha</s>) and [inference] for the sake of another (<s>parārtha</s>). In that regard, proof is inference for the sake of another, while this [i.e., inference proper] is for one's own sake. But another says: 'The mention of proof and refutation at the outset is inappropriate, since their application is preceded by perception and inference.' It is replied: Even though those [perception and inference] precede [proof and refutation], since the commencement of the treatise has as its primary [aim] the cognition of another (<s>parasaṃvit</s>), and since proof and refutation also have that as their result, their presentation at the beginning [is justified] due to proximity [to the main purpose]. Others [say that] inference for one's own sake is dependent on [inference] for the sake of another — [thus the ordering is] for the purpose of demonstrating the method of reasoning.

body.text: kṛtaṃ prasaṅgena / prakṛtaṃ prastumaḥ // iha ca sādhanādayo 'ṣṭau padārthāḥ abhidheyatayā uktāḥ / parasaṃvittyātmasaṃvittyoratra prayojanatvena saṃbandhaśca sāmarthyagamya eva / sa ca kāryakāraṇalakṣaṇaḥ / kāraṇaṃ vacanarūpāpannaprakaraṇameva / kāryaṃ tu prakaraṇārthaparijñānam / tathāhīdamasya kāryamiti saṃbandhalakṣaṇā ṣaṣṭhī / āha- yadyevaṃ parasaṃvittyātmasaṃvittyoḥ prakaraṇārthaparijñānena vyavahitatvādaprayojanatvamiti / na / vyavahitasyaiva vivakṣitatvāt / kimarthaṃ vyavahitameva vivakṣitamiti / ucyate / uttarottaraprayojanānāṃ prādhānyakhyāpanārtham / tathā cehānuttaraprayojanaṃ paramagatiprāptireva / tathā coktam /
body.translated_text: Enough of this digression. Let us resume the main topic. Here, proof and the other eight categories (<s>padārtha</s>s) have been stated as the subject matter. The relation between the cognition of another (<s>parasaṃvit</s>) and self-cognition (<s>ātmasaṃvit</s>) [on the one hand] and [these categories on the other] is stated here as the purpose, and the connection is to be understood through capacity [alone]. And that [connection] has the nature of cause and effect. The cause is the text (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) itself as presented in the form of words. The effect, however, is the full comprehension of the meaning of the text. Thus [the genitive in the sūtra] is a genitive denoting relation, [meaning:] 'this is the effect of that.' One might object: 'If so, since the cognition of another and self-cognition are separated [from the immediate subject] by the full comprehension of the text's meaning, they are not the purpose [of the treatise].' No, because it is precisely the remote [purpose] that is intended. For what reason is the remote [purpose] alone intended? It is replied: for the purpose of indicating the primacy of successively higher purposes. And thus the ultimate purpose here is none other than the attainment of the supreme goal (<s>paramagati</s>). As it has been said:

children.translated_text: Through correct comprehension of reasoning, knowing what is to be accepted and what is to be rejected,
having accepted what is to be accepted, they attain the supreme goal (<s>paramā gati</s>).

body.text: āha- yadyevamihānuttaramevedaṃ kasmānnopanyastamiti / ucyate / avyutpannaṃ vineyagaṇamadhikṛtya tatprathamatayaiva tasyāprayojakatvāt // aparastvāha / idamiha śrotaṇāṃ prayojanamuktaṃ kartustarhi kiṃ prayojanamiti vācyam / ucyate / tasyāpyanantaraparabhedabhinnamidameva / anantaraṃ tāvatsattvānugrahaḥ / paraṃparaṃ tu paramagatiprāptireva / tathā coktam /
body.translated_text: One might object: 'If so, since this [supreme goal] is the ultimate [purpose] here, why was it not stated [explicitly]?' It is replied: because, taking into consideration the audience of uninstructed disciples, [the supreme goal] would not serve as a motivating [purpose] for them at the very outset. Another says: 'This purpose for the listeners has been stated; what then is the purpose for the author? This should be stated.' It is replied: his [purpose] too is this very same [thing], differentiated into immediate and remote aspects. The immediate [purpose] is the benefiting of beings. The remote [purpose], however, is nothing other than the attainment of the supreme goal. As it has been said:

children.translated_text: He who, through correct instruction in reasoning, benefits beings
who are outside the [path of] reasoning — he attains the auspicious (<s>śiva</s>) state before long.

body.text: alaṃ vistareṇa //
body.translated_text: Enough of elaboration.

body.text: iti śāstrasaṃgrahaḥ / itiśabdaḥ parisamāptivācakaḥ / etāvāneva / śiṣyate 'nena tattvamiti śāstramadhikṛtameva; arya(rthya)ta ityarthaḥ / śāstrasyārthaḥ śāstrārthaḥ / tasya sagrahaḥ śāstrārthasaṃgrahaḥ / saṃgrahaṇaṃ saṃgrahaḥ / etāvānevādhikṛtaśāstrārthasaṃkṣepa ityarthaḥ / śāstrato cāsyālpagranthasyāpi viśvavyāpakanyāyānuśāsanāditi vṛddhavādaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the summary of the <s>śāstra</s>. The word 'thus' (<s>iti</s>) denotes completion. 'Only this much' — the <s>śāstra</s> that is investigated is precisely what is to be sought; that is the meaning. The meaning of the <s>śāstra</s> is <s>śāstrārtha</s>. Its compendium (<s>saṃgraha</s>) is the <s>śāstrārthasaṃgraha</s>. 'Compiling' (<s>saṃgrahaṇa</s>) is 'compendium' (<s>saṃgraha</s>). The meaning is: only this much is the summary of the meaning of the investigated <s>śāstra</s>. And from the [larger] <s>śāstra</s>, this is [a work] of small compass...

body.text: tatra yathoddeśastathā nirdeśa iti kṛtvā sādhanasvarūpāvadhāraṇāyāha // tatra pakṣādivacanāni sādhanam / tatraśabdo nirdhāraṇārthaḥ / tatra teṣu sādhanādiṣu sādhanaṃ tāvannirdhāryate iti / nirdhāraṇaṃ ca jātiguṇakriyānimittamiti / atra guṇanimittaṃ sādhanatvena guṇena nirdhāryate iti / gomaṇḍalādiva gauḥ kṣīrasaṃpannatvena guṇena // pacyate iti pakṣaḥ / paca vyaktīkaraṇe / pacyate vyaktīkriyate yo 'rthaḥ sa pakṣaḥ / sādhya ityarthaḥ / sa ca dharmaviśiṣṭo dharmī / pakṣa ādiryeṣāṃ te pakṣādayaḥ / ayaṃ bahubrīhiḥ samāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, following the principle 'the exposition should follow the order of the enumeration,' in order to ascertain the nature of proof (<s>sādhana</s>), [the text] states: 'Therein, the statements [beginning with] the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) etc. constitute the proof.' The word 'therein' (<s>tatra</s>) has the sense of determination (<s>nirdhāraṇa</s>) — 'among those [items such as] proof etc., the proof is first to be determined.' And determination is based on class (<s>jāti</s>), quality (<s>guṇa</s>), and action (<s>kriyā</s>). Here, [the determination is] by quality — it is determined by the quality of 'being a proof.' Like from a herd of cows...

body.text: ayaṃ ca tadguṇasaṃvijñānaśca bhavati / tatra tadguṇasaṃvijñāno yathā lambakarṇa ityādi / lambau karṇau yasyāsau lambakarṇaḥ / lambakarṇatvaṃ ca tasyaiva guṇa ityarthaḥ / atadguṇasaṃvijñāno yathā parvatādikaṃ kṣetramityādi / parvata ādiryasya tatparvatādikaṃ kṣetram / na parvataḥ kṣetraguṇaḥ / kiṃ tarhi / upalakṣaṇamātramiti bhāvanā /
body.translated_text: And this [compound] is also one whose designation is known by that quality (<s>tadguṇasaṃvijñāna</s>). There, an example of [a compound] whose designation is known by that quality is '<s>lambakarṇa</s>' (long-eared) etc. — he whose ears are long is <s>lambakarṇa</s>; and 'long-earedness' is precisely a quality of that [thing]; that is the meaning. An example of [a compound] whose designation is not known by that quality (<s>atadguṇasaṃvijñāna</s>) is 'a field with mountains etc.' — a field whose foremost [feature] is a mountain is 'a field with mountains etc.' The mountain is not a quality of the field. Rather...

body.text: ayamiha tadguṇasaṃvijñāno bahuvrīhirveditavyaḥ / yathā parvatādikaṃ kṣetraṃ nadyādikaṃ vanamiti / na punaryathā lambakarṇaḥ brāhmaṇādayo varṇā iti / pakṣādivacanāni sādhanamityādiśabda upalakṣaṇārthaḥ / asya cāyamarthaḥ / ādīyate 'smādityādiḥ yathā parvatādikaṃ kṣetramityādau / na punarādīyate ityādiḥ yathā brāhmaṇādayo varṇā ityadāviti / tataḥ susthitamidaṃ pakṣaḥ ādiryeṣāṃ te pakṣādayaḥ // te ca pakṣopalakṣitā hetudṛṣṭāntāḥ / teṣāṃ vacanānyuktayaḥ // kiṃ sādhanamiti /
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound whose designation is known by that quality should be understood as in 'a field with mountains, a forest with rivers' — but not as in '<s>lambakarṇa</s>' or '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and other <s>varṇa</s>s.' The word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>) in 'the statements [beginning with] the thesis etc. constitute the proof' serves the purpose of indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>). And the meaning of this is as follows: '[that from which] something is taken' is <s>ādi</s> (beginning), as in 'a field with mountains etc.' — but not [the sense in which] '<s>ādi</s>' means 'beginning' [alone]...

body.text: iha ca yadā sādhyate 'neneti sādhanaṃ karaṇābhidhānārthaḥ sādhanaśabdastadā pakṣopalakṣitāni hetutvādivacanāni sādhanam / yatastaiḥ karaṇabhūtairvivakṣito 'rthaḥ parasaṃtāne pratipādyate / yadā punarbhāvasādhanaḥ siddhiḥ sādhanamiti tadā pakṣādivacanajanyaṃ pratipādyagataṃ jñānameva sādhanam / tatphalatvātpakṣādivacanānām / kārye kāraṇopacārāt / yathedaṃ me śarīraṃ paurāṇāṃ karmeti / yadā tu kartṛsādhanaḥ sādhayatīti sādhanaṃ tadā pakṣādivacanānyeva kartṛtvena vivakṣyante pratipādyasaṃtāne jñānotpādakatvāt iti / tadevaṃ pakṣādivacanāni sādhanam / tadyathā vṛkṣā vanaṃ hastyādayaḥ senā / āha / ekavacananirdeśaḥ kimarthamucyate / samuditānāmeva pakṣādivacanānāṃ sādhanatvakhyāpanārtham / uktaṃ ca diṅnāgācāryeṇa sādhanamiti caikavacananirdeśaḥ samastasādhanatvakhyāpanārthaḥ / ityalaṃ vistareṇa //
body.translated_text: Now here, when the word <s>sādhana</s> (proof) is used in the instrumental sense (<s>karaṇābhidhāna</s>) — 'that by which [something] is established' — then the statements about the logical reason (<s>hetu</s>) etc., qualified by the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>), constitute the proof. For by these, as instrumental means, the intended meaning is established in the opponent's mind. But when <s>sādhana</s> is used in the sense of 'accomplishment' (<s>siddhi</s>) — 'establishment is proof' — then the proof is the knowledge itself, born from the statements of thesis etc., arising in the person to be convinced. And its result...

body.text: evaṃ tāvatsāmānyena sādhanamuktam / idaṃ ca na jñāyate kiṃ kārakamuta vyañjakam / sādhanasya dvaividhyadarśanāt / tatra kārakaṃ vījādyaṅkurādeḥ / vyañjakaṃ pradīpādi tamasi ghaṭādīnām / ato vyañjakatvapratipādanāyāha / pakṣahetudṛṣṭāntavacanairhi prāśnikānāmapratīto 'rthaḥ pratipādyate iti // asya gamanikā / pacyate iti pakṣaḥ / hinotīti hetuḥ / hi gatau / sarve gatyarthāḥ jñānārthāḥ / tathā dṛṣṭamarthamantaṃ nayatīti dṛṣṭāntaḥ / sa ca dvidhā sādharmyevaidharmyabhedāt / tataścaivaṃ samāsaḥ / dṛṣṭāntaśca dṛṣṭāntaśca dṛṣṭāntau / hetuśca dṛṣṭāntau ca hetudṛṣṭāntāḥ / pakṣasya hetudṛṣṭāntāḥ pakṣahetudṛṣṭāntāḥ / teṣāṃ vacanāni pakṣahetudṛṣṭāntavacanāni / taiḥ pakṣahetudṛṣṭāntavacanaiḥ / hiśabdo yasmādarthe / praśneniyuktāḥ prāśnikā vidvāṃsaḥ / svasamayaparasamayavedinaḥ / uktaṃ ca-
body.translated_text: Thus, proof (<s>sādhana</s>) has been stated in general terms. And this is not known: is it productive (<s>kāraka</s>) or revelatory (<s>vyañjaka</s>)? — since proof is seen to be of two kinds. In that regard, the productive [type] is like a seed for a sprout and so on. The revelatory [type] is like a lamp for a pot and so on in darkness. Therefore, in order to establish its revelatory nature, he says: 'For by means of statements of thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>), reason (<s>hetu</s>), and example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>), a meaning not [yet] understood by the examiners (<s>prāśnikas</s>) is made known.' The etymological analysis of this is as follows: that which is examined (<s>pacyate</s>) is the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis). That which removes [ignorance] (<s>hinotīti</s>) is the <s>hetu</s> (reason) — from the root <s>hi</s> meaning 'to go'; all roots meaning movement also mean knowledge. Likewise, that which leads one to the end of a seen meaning is the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example). And that is of two kinds, due to the distinction between [examples by] similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) and dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>). And the compound [analysis] is thus: example and example are 'two examples' (<s>dṛṣṭāntau</s>); reason and the two examples are 'reason-and-examples' (<s>hetudṛṣṭāntāḥ</s>); the reason-and-examples of the thesis are 'thesis-reason-examples' (<s>pakṣahetudṛṣṭāntāḥ</s>); their statements are 'thesis-reason-example-statements' (<s>pakṣahetudṛṣṭāntavacanāni</s>); by those thesis-reason-example-statements. The word <s>hi</s> is used in the sense of 'because' (<s>yasmāt</s>). Those engaged by questioning are <s>prāśnikas</s>, i.e., learned ones — those who know their own and others' doctrinal systems. And it has been said:

body.text: svasamayaparasamayajñāḥ kulajāḥ pakṣadvayasthitāḥ kṣamiṇaḥ / vādapatheṣvabhiyuktāstulāsamāḥ prāśnikāḥ proktāḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Those who know their own and others' doctrinal systems, of good family, established in both sides [of a debate], patient, skilled in the paths of disputation, impartial like a balance — they are called examiners (<s>prāśnikas</s>).'

body.text: teṣāṃ prāśnikānāmapratīto 'navagato 'navabuddho 'rthaḥ pratipādyate / āha / ye yathoktāḥ prāśnikāḥ kathaṃ teṣāṃ kaścidapratīto 'rtha iti / ucyate / na tatparijñānamaṅgīkṛtyāpratītaḥ / kiṃtu vādiprativādipakṣaparigrahasamarthanāsahastadantargata ityato 'pratīto 'rthaḥ pratipādyate / nanu cātra cāturthyā kriyayā ceti vaktavyalakṣaṇayā bhavitavyaṃ tatkimartha ṣaṣṭhyatrocyate / kārakāṇāmavivakṣā śeṣa iti śeṣalakṣaṇā ṣaṣṭhī / keṣāṃ pratipādyate / sāmarthyādyeṣāmapratītaḥ anyeṣāmaśrutatvātteṣāmeva pratipādyate /
body.translated_text: For those examiners (<s>prāśnikas</s>), a meaning that is not understood, not comprehended, not cognized, is made known. [Objection:] He says — those who are described as examiners, how could any meaning be not understood by them? [Reply:] It is said — it is not 'not understood' in the sense of acknowledging their complete knowledge [of it]; rather, because it is contained within the capacity to support the adoption of the positions of proponent (<s>vādin</s>) and opponent (<s>prativādin</s>), therefore the 'not-understood' meaning is made known. [Objection:] Now, here the dative case and the verb should be in accordance with the rule to be stated — so why is the genitive used here? [Reply:] It is said — when the agent-factors (<s>kārakas</s>) are not intended to be expressed, the remainder is [expressed by] the genitive, which has the characteristic of 'the rest' (<s>śeṣa</s>). [Question:] For whom is it made known? [Reply:] By implication, it is made known precisely for those for whom [the meaning] is not understood, not for others, since they have not heard [the argument].

body.text: itiśabdastasmādarthe / yasmādevaṃ tasmādvyañjakamidaṃ sādhanamapratītārthapratipādakatvāt pradīpavat / vyatireke bījādi // tatra pakṣādivacanāni sādhanam ityuiktam // adhunā yathoddeśaṃ nirdeśa itinyāyamāśritya pakṣalakṣaṇapratipādanāyāha / tatra pakṣaḥ prasiddho dharmī / asya gamanikā / tatraśabdo nirdhāraṇārthaḥ / nirdhāraṇaṃ ca prasiddhadharmitvādiguṇato 'vaseyamiti / pakṣa iti lakṣyanirdeśaḥ / dharmīti / dharmāḥ kṛtakatvādayaste 'sya vidyante iti dharmī śabdādiḥ / kathaṃ prasiddha ityata āha / prasiddhaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭatayā svayaṃ sādhyatvenepsitaḥ / tatra prasiddhaṃ vādiprativādibhyāṃ pramāṇabalena pratipannam / viśiṣyate 'neneti viśeṣaṇam / tena viśiṣṭaḥ prasiddhaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭaḥ /
body.translated_text: The word <s>iti</s> is used in the sense of 'therefore' (<s>tasmāt</s>). Since this is so, therefore this proof is revelatory (<s>vyañjaka</s>), because it makes known a meaning not [previously] understood — like a lamp. In the negative case [it would be] like a seed and so on. Therein, it has been said that the statements of thesis and so on constitute proof (<s>sādhana</s>). Now, following the principle that 'the detailed exposition follows the order of the summary listing,' in order to set forth the definition of the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>), he says: 'Therein, the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) is a well-known property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>).' The analysis of this is as follows: the word 'therein' (<s>tatra</s>) is for the purpose of specification (<s>nirdhāraṇa</s>). And the specification is to be understood from the quality of being a well-known property-bearer and so on. '<s>Pakṣa</s>' is the indication of the definiendum (<s>lakṣya</s>). '<s>Dharmin</s>' (property-bearer) means: <s>dharmas</s> (properties) such as being-produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) and the like belong to it — hence [it is called] <s>dharmin</s>, such as sound and so on. [Question:] How is it 'well-known' (<s>prasiddha</s>)? To this he says: 'As qualified by a well-known qualifier, it is desired by oneself as that which is to be proved.' Therein, 'well-known' means apprehended by the force of a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) by both the proponent and the opponent. That by which [something] is qualified is a qualifier (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>). That which is qualified by it is 'qualified by a well-known qualifier' (<s>prasiddhaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭa</s>).

body.text: tadbhāvaḥ prasiddhaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭatatā / tayā prasiddhaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭatayā hetubhūtayā prasiddhaḥ / atrāha / iha dharmiṇastāvatprasiddhatā yuktā viśeṣaṇasya tvanityatvāderna yujyate / sādhyatvāt / anyathā vivādābhāvena sādhanaprayogānupapatteḥ / naitadevam / samyagarthānavabodhāt / iha prasiddhatā viśeṣaṇasya na tasminneva dharmiṇi samāśrīyate kiṃtu dharmyantare ghaṭādau / tataśca yathoktadoṣānupapattiḥ / tathā svayamityanenābhyupagamasiddhāntaparigrahaḥ // sādhyatvenepsita iti / sādhanīyaḥ sādhayitavyaḥ sādhanamarhatīti vā sādhyaḥ / tasya bhāvaḥ sādhyatvama / tena sādhyatvena / īpsitaḥ abhimataḥ iṣṭa icchāyā vyāpta ityarthaḥ / iha ca viśeṣaṇasya vyavacchedakatvātprasiddho dharmītyanenāprasiddhaviśeṣaṇasya pakṣābhāsasya vyavacchedo draṣṭavyaḥ / prasiddhaviśepaṇaviśiṣṭayetyanena tvaprasiddhaviśeṣaṇasya ubhayena cāprasiddhobhayasya svayamityanena cābhyupagamasiddhāntaparigraheṇa sarvatantrapratitantrādhikaraṇasiddhāntānāṃ vyavacchedo draṣṭavyaḥ / iha tu śastranirapekṣavādinorlokaprasiddhayordharmadharmiṇoḥ parigrahavacanamabhyupagamasiddhāntastaṃ svayamityanenāha / tataścayadapi svayamiti vādinā yastadā sādhanamāha / etena yadyapi kvacicchāstre sthtiaḥ sādhanamāha tacchāstrakāreṇa tasmindharmiṇyanekadharmābhyupagame 'pi yastadānena vādinā dharmaḥ sādhayitumiṣṭaḥ sa eva sādhyo netara ityuktaṃ bhavatīti yaduktaṃ vādimukhyena tadapi saṃgatameva / sādhyatveneti sādhyatvenaiva na sādhanatvenāpi / anena ca sādhyahetudṛṣṭāntābhāsānāṃ pakṣatvavyudāsaḥ / īpsita ityanena ca noktamātrasyaivetyuktaṃ bhavati / icchayāpi vyāptaḥ pakṣaḥ / ityetacca parārthāścakṣurādaya ityatra darśayiṣyāmaḥ / ityanena dharmaviśiṣṭo dharmī pakṣa ityāveditaṃ bhavati / tataśca na dharmamātraṃ na dharmī kevalaḥ na svatantramubhayaṃ na ca tayoḥ saṃbandhaḥ kiṃtu dharmadharmiṇorviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāva iti bhāvārthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Its nature' (<s>tadbhāva</s>) means being qualified by a well-established qualifier (<s>prasiddhaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭatā</s>). By that — i.e., by being qualified by a well-established qualifier, which serves as the ground — [the <s>dharmin</s>, property-possessor, is] well-established. Here an objection is raised: In this [definition], the well-establishedness of the <s>dharmin</s> (property-possessor) is appropriate; but the well-establishedness of the qualifier — such as impermanence and the like — is not appropriate, because it is what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>). Otherwise, there would be no dispute, and the application of a proof would be unjustified. This is not so, due to a failure to properly understand the meaning. Here, the well-establishedness of the qualifier is not taken as [established] in that very <s>dharmin</s>, but rather in another <s>dharmin</s> such as a pot and so on. And thus the stated defect does not arise. Likewise, by the word 'oneself' (<s>svayam</s>), the acceptance of the <s>abhyupagamasiddhānta</s> (a principle accepted for the sake of argument) is indicated. 'Desired as that which is to be proved' (<s>sādhyatvenepsita</s>): <s>sādhya</s> means 'that which is to be established,' 'that which ought to be established,' or 'that which deserves proof.' Its nature is <s>sādhyatva</s> (the status of being that which is to be proved). By that <s>sādhyatva</s> — <s>īpsita</s> means 'intended,' 'desired,' 'pervaded by wish' — this is the meaning. And here, since the qualifier (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>) functions as the distinguishing element, by [the phrase] 'a well-established <s>dharmin</s>' the exclusion of the thesis-semblance (<s>pakṣābhāsa</s>) having an unestablished qualifier is to be seen. But by [the phrase] 'qualified by a well-established qualifier,' the exclusion of [the semblance with] an unestablished qualifier and — by both [qualifications combined] — [the semblance with] both [<s>dharmin</s> and qualifier] unestablished [are excluded]; and by 'oneself' (<s>svayam</s>), by means of the acceptance of the <s>abhyupagamasiddhānta</s>, the exclusion of the <s>sarvatantrasiddhānta</s> (a principle accepted by all schools), <s>pratitantrasiddhānta</s> (a principle accepted by one's own school), and <s>adhikaraṇasiddhānta</s> (a principle established for the purpose of argument) is to be seen. Here, however, the statement of acceptance of a <s>dharma</s> (property) and <s>dharmin</s> (property-possessor) that are well-known to the speaker and [opponent] independently of scripture is the <s>abhyupagamasiddhānta</s> — [this] he states by 'oneself' (<s>svayam</s>). And thus, even though someone who states a proof based on a [certain] scripture — even though in that scripture many properties are accepted with respect to that <s>dharmin</s> — the property which that speaker intends to prove is alone the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved), not any other — this is what is stated. And what has been said by the chief proponent is also entirely consistent. 'By <s>sādhyatva</s>' means 'by <s>sādhyatva</s> alone — not also by the status of being a means of proof (<s>sādhanatva</s>).' And by this, the exclusion of semblances of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), <s>hetu</s> (reason), and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) from being a <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) [is achieved]. And by '<s>īpsita</s>' (desired), it is stated that not merely what is verbally stated [qualifies], but the <s>pakṣa</s> must also be pervaded by intention (<s>icchā</s>). And this we shall demonstrate in [the discussion of] 'the eyes and the like are for the sake of another.' By the word <s>iti</s> ('thus'), it is indicated that the <s>dharmin</s> qualified by a <s>dharma</s> is the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis). And thus, neither the <s>dharma</s> alone, nor the <s>dharmin</s> alone, nor both independently, nor the relation between them — but rather the qualifier-qualificand relationship (<s>viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāva</s>) of <s>dharma</s> and <s>dharmin</s> — this is the intended meaning.

body.text: iha coktalakṣaṇayoge satyapyaśrāvaṇaḥ śabda ityevamādīnāmapi pratyakṣāviruddhānāṃ pakṣatvaprāptyātivyāptirnāma lakṣaṇadoṣaḥ prāpnotītyastannivṛttyarthamāha / pratyakṣādyaviruddha iti vākyaśeṣaḥ / pratyakṣādibhiraviruddhaḥ / ādiśabdādanuktānumānādiparigrahaḥ / ityayaṃ vākyaśeṣo vākyādhyāhāro draṣṭavya iti / udāharaṇopadarśanāyāha tadyathā / anityaḥ śabdo nityo veti / tadyathetyudāharaṇopanyāsārtham / tatra bauddhāderanityaḥ śabdo vaiyākaraṇādernitya iti / ukta sodāharaṇaḥ pakṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: Now, even when the stated definition is satisfied, the following objection arises: propositions such as 'sound is inaudible' (<s>aśrāvaṇaḥ śabdaḥ</s>), which are not contradicted by perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), would also obtain the status of a <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) — and this constitutes the definitional defect called over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>). In order to preclude this, [the author] states the remainder of the sentence: 'not contradicted by perception and the rest' (<s>pratyakṣādyaviruddha</s>). [This means:] not contradicted by perception and the rest. By the word 'and the rest' (<s>ādi</s>), the inclusion of [the means of knowledge] not [explicitly] mentioned — such as inference and the like — is [indicated]. This remainder of the sentence, or sentence-supplement, is to be understood [as part of the definition]. To illustrate with an example, [the author] says 'for instance' (<s>tadyathā</s>): 'Sound is impermanent' or 'Sound is permanent.' The word <s>tadyathā</s> is for the purpose of introducing examples. Among these, 'Sound is impermanent' is [the thesis] of the Buddhists and others; 'Sound is permanent' is [the thesis] of the grammarians and others. Thus the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) has been stated with examples.

body.text: sāṃprataṃ hetumabhidhitsurāha hetustrirūpaḥ / tatra hinoti gamayati jijñāsitadharmaviśiṣṭānarthāniti hetuḥ / sa ca trirūpaḥ / trīṇi rūpāṇi yasyāsau trirūpaḥ trisvabhāva ityarthaḥ / ekasya vastuno nānātvamapaśyan pṛcchaka āha kiṃ punastrirūpyam / kimiti paripraśne / punariti vitarke / trirūpasya bhāvastrairūpyam / evaṃ pṛcchakena pṛṣṭaḥ sannāhācāryaḥ pakṣadharmatvaṃ sapakṣe sattvaṃ vipakṣe cāsattvameva / asya gamanikā / uktalakṣaṇaḥ pakṣatasya dharmaḥ pakṣadharmastadbhāvaḥ pakṣadharmatvam / pakṣaśabdena cātra kevalo dharmyeva 'bhidhīyate / avayave samudāyopacārāt / idamekaṃ rūpam / tathā sapakṣe sattvam / sapakṣo vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇaḥ / tasminsattvamastitvaṃ sāmānyena bhāva ityarthaḥ / idaṃ dvitīyaṃ rūpam / tathā vipakṣe cāsattvamiti tṛtīyaṃ rūpam / vipakṣo vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇastasminpunarasattvamevāvidyamānataiva / caśabdaḥ punaḥśabdārthaḥ / sa ca viśeṣārtha iti darśitameva / āha ihaivāvadhāraṇe 'bhidhānaṃ kimartham / ucyate / atraivaikāntāsattvapratipādanārtham /
body.translated_text: Now, intending to state the <s>hetu</s> (reason/logical mark), he says: 'The <s>hetu</s> has three characteristics (<s>trirūpa</s>).' Therein, <s>hetu</s> means 'that which propels or leads one to know objects qualified by the property under investigation' — thus it is the reason. And it has three characteristics (<s>trirūpa</s>): that which has three forms — that is <s>trirūpa</s>, meaning 'of three natures.' A questioner, not seeing how a single entity can have multiplicity, asks: 'What then is the triple-characterization?' <s>kim</s> is for inquiry; <s>punar</s> is for deliberation. The state of being <s>trirūpa</s> (having three forms) is <s>trairūpya</s> (triple-characterization). Thus questioned by the questioner, the <s>Ācārya</s> (master) says: 'Being a property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharmatva</s>), presence in the homologous instances (<s>sapakṣe sattva</s>), and absence only in the heterologous instances (<s>vipakṣe asattva</s>).' The explanation of this is as follows: the property of [something] whose stated definition is the thesis — that is <s>pakṣadharma</s> (property of the thesis-subject); the state of being that is <s>pakṣadharmatva</s>. And by the word <s>pakṣa</s> here, only the bare <s>dharmin</s> (property-possessor) is denoted, by figurative application of the whole to a part. This is the first form. Likewise, 'presence in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologous instance)': the <s>sapakṣa</s> has the definition to be stated [below]; presence in it means existence, having [the property] generally — this is the meaning. This is the second form. Likewise, 'and absence in the <s>vipakṣa</s> (heterologous instance)' — this is the third form. The <s>vipakṣa</s> has the definition to be stated; and absence in it means non-existence only. The word <s>ca</s> has the meaning of <s>punar</s> ('moreover'). And it serves a specifying function — as has been shown. One asks: What is the purpose of the restriction here? It is said: For the purpose of establishing that there is absolute absence [in the <s>vipakṣa</s>].

body.text: sapakṣe tvekadeśe 'pi sattvamaduṣṭameveti / tathā ca satyekāntato vipakṣavyāvṛttāḥ sapakṣaikadeśavyāpino 'pi prayatnānantarīyakatvādayaḥ samyagghetava evetyāveditaṃ bhavati // sapakṣe sattvamityādi yaduktaṃ tatra sapakṣavipakṣayoḥ svarūpamajānāno vineyaḥ pṛcchati / kaḥ punaḥ sapakṣaḥ ko vā vipakṣa iti / ayaṃ tu praśno nigadasiddha eva / nirvacanaṃ tvidaṃ sādhyadharmetyādi / asya gamanikā / ihopacāravṛttyā dharme sādhyatvamadhikṛtyocyate / sādhyaścāsau dharmaśca sādhyadharmaḥ / anityatvādiḥ / samānaḥ sadṛśastasya bhāvaḥ sāmānyaṃ tulyatā / sādhyadharmasya sādhyadharmeṇa vā sāmānyaṃ sādhyadharmasāmānyam / tena samāno 'rthaḥ sapakṣa iti / samaṃ tulyaṃ mānamasyeti samānaḥ / tulyamānaparicchedya iti bhāvanā / artho ghaṭādiḥ / na tu vacanamātram / samānaḥ pakṣaṃ sapakṣa iti / athavā upacāravṛttyā dharmiṇi sādhyatvamadhikriyate /
body.translated_text: But in the <s>sapakṣa</s>, even presence in a part is quite unobjectionable. And accordingly, [reasons] such as 'being produced immediately after effort,' which are absolutely excluded from the <s>vipakṣa</s> and pervade only a part of the <s>sapakṣa</s>, are communicated as being valid reasons (<s>samyaghetu</s>). Regarding what was stated — 'presence in the <s>sapakṣa</s>' and so on — therein, a trainee not knowing the nature of <s>sapakṣa</s> and <s>vipakṣa</s> asks: 'What then is the <s>sapakṣa</s>? And what is the <s>vipakṣa</s>?' But this question is already settled by the running text. However, the etymological derivation (<s>nirvacana</s>) is as follows: 'The property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharma</s>)...' and so on. The explanation of this: here, by figurative usage, it is the property that is spoken of as being 'to be proved.' And that which is both to-be-proved and a property is the <s>sādhyadharma</s> — [namely] impermanence and the like. <s>Samāna</s> means 'similar'; its state is <s>sāmānya</s>, meaning similarity or equality. The similarity of the <s>sādhyadharma</s> — or with the <s>sādhyadharma</s> — is <s>sādhyadharmasāmānya</s>. An object that is <s>samāna</s> (similar) by that [similarity] is a <s>sapakṣa</s>. <s>Samāna</s> means: 'that which has an equal measure' — the idea is: 'to be determined by an equal standard.' The object [here means] a pot and the like — not a mere statement. That which is <s>samāna</s> (similar) to the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) is a <s>sapakṣa</s>. Alternatively, by figurative usage, it is the <s>dharmin</s> (property-possessor) that is spoken of as 'to be proved.'

body.text: tataśca / sādhyasya dharmaḥ sādhyadharmaḥ / śeṣaṃ pūrvavat / anupacaritaṃ tu sādhyam / dharmaviśiṣṭo dharmīti bhāvārthaḥ // sāṃprataṃ sapakṣasyaiva udāharaṇamupadarśayannāha / tadyathā anitye śabde sādhye ityādi / tadyathetyudāharaṇopanyāsārthaḥ / anitye śabde sādhye kim? / ghaṭādiranityaḥ padārthasaṃghātaḥ sapakṣaḥ / sādhyānityātvasamānatvāt // adhunā vipalakṣaṇapratipādanāyāha / vipakṣo yatra sādhyaṃ nāsti / visadṛśaḥ pakṣo vipakṣaḥ / sa kīdṛgiti svarūpato darśayati / yatra yasminnarthe / sādhanīyaṃ sādhyam / nāsti na vidyate / iha ca sādhyapratibandhatvāt sādhanasya tadapi nāstīti gamyate / udāharaṇaṃ darśayati / yathā yannityamityādi / tatra yannityamiti kimuktaṃ bhavati? / yadanityaṃ na bhavati tadakṛtakaṃ dṛṣṭamiti / tatkṛtakamapi na dṛṣṭam yathākāśamiti / tatra hi sādhyabhāvāt sādhanābhāvaḥ / sāṃprataṃ vicitratvādavadhāraṇavidheḥ vipakṣadharmatvādiṣu tamupadarśayannāha / tatra kṛtakatvamityādi / tatreti pūrvavat / kṛtakatvaṃ prayatnānantarīyakatvaṃ vā anityādau heturiti yogaḥ / tatra kriyate iti kṛtakaḥ / apekṣitaparavyāpāro hi bhāvaḥ svabhāvaniṣpattau kṛtaka iti / tadbhāvaḥ kṛtakatvam / prayatnāntarīyakatvaṃ vā iti / prayatnaścetanāvato vyāpāraḥ / tasya prayatnānantaraṃ tatra bhāvo jāta iti vā prayatnānantarīyaḥ / sa eva prayatnānantarīyakaḥ / tadbhāvaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvam /
body.translated_text: And therefore: the property of what is to be proved is the 'property to be proved' (<s>sādhyadharma</s>). The rest is as before. But 'what is to be proved' (<s>sādhya</s>) is [used here in its] literal [sense]. The intended meaning is: the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) is that which is qualified by the property. Now, showing an example of the similar case (<s>sapakṣa</s>) alone, [the text] states: 'For example, when impermanence of sound is to be proved,' etc. '<s>Tadyathā</s>' (for example) serves the purpose of presenting an illustration. When sound is to be proved impermanent — what [is the <s>sapakṣa</s>]? A pot and the like — an impermanent aggregate of entities — is the similar case (<s>sapakṣa</s>), because of possessing the same [property of] impermanence as that which is to be proved. Now, in order to teach the definition of the dissimilar case (<s>vipakṣa</s>), [the text] states: 'The dissimilar case (<s>vipakṣa</s>) is where that [property]...'

body.text: vāśabdaḥ caśabdārthaḥ / sa ca samuccaye / dvitīyahetvabhidhānaṃ vipakṣavyāvṛttaḥ / sapakṣaikadeśavṛttirapi samyaggheturyathā / yameveti darśanārthatvādaduṣṭamiti / ayaṃ ca hetuḥ kiṃ pakṣadharma eva na tu pakṣasyaiva dharmaḥ / ayogavyavacchedamātraphalatvādavadhāraṇasya / yathā caitro dhanurdhara eva / anena cāsiddhānāṃ caturṇāmasādhāraṇasya ca vyāvṛttiḥ / tathā saphala evāstvanyayogavyavacchedaḥ yathā pārtha eva dhanurdharaḥ / anena tu sādhāraṇādīnāṃ navānāmapi hetvābhāsānāṃ vyāvṛttiḥ / āha / yadi sapakṣa evāsti tataśca tadvyatirekeṇānyatra pakṣe 'pyabhāvāt dharmatvānupapattiḥ / na anavadhṛtāvadhāraṇāt / pakṣadharmatvasyāvadhāritvāt / āha / yadyevaṃ vipakṣe nāsti eveti tṛtīyamavadhāraṇaṃ kimartham? / ucyate / prayogopadarśanārtham / uktaṃ ca / anvayavyatirekayorekamapi rūpamuktaṃ kathaṃ nu nāma dvitīyasyākṣepakaṃ syāditi / prabhūtamatra vaktavyaṃ tattu nocyate / granthavistarabhayāt / gamanikāmātnametat / anityādau heturityatrādigrahaṇāt duḥkhādiparigrahaḥ / ityukto hetuḥ // sāṃprataṃ dṛṣṭāntamabhidhitsurāha / dṛṣṭānta ityādi / dṛṣṭaṃ tatrārthaṃ antaṃ nayatīti dṛṣṭāntaḥ / pramāṇopalabdhameva vipratipattau saṃvedananiṣṭhāṃ nayatītyarthaḥ / sa ca dvividhaḥ / dve vidhe yasya sa dvividhastadeva dvaividhyam / darśayati sādharmyeṇa vaidharmyeṇa ca / samāno dharmo yasyāsau sadharmā sadharmaṇo bhāvaḥ sādharmyaṃ tena / visadṛśo dharmo yasyāsau vidharmā vidharmaṇo bhāvaḥ vaidharmyaṃ tena / caśabdaḥ samuccaye / tatra sādharmyeṇa tāvaditi / tāvacchabdaḥ kramārthaḥ / yatreti / abhidheyahetoruktalakṣaṇasya sapakṣa evāstitvaṃ khyāpyate / sapakṣa uktalakṣaṇastasmiṃścāstitvaṃ vidyamānatvaṃ khyāpyate pratipādyate vacanena / taccedam / yatkṛtakaṃ tadanityaṃ yathā ghaṭādiḥ iti sugamam / anena sādhanadṛṣṭāntābhāsaḥ / vaidharmyeṇāpi / yatra sādhyābhāve hetorabhāva eva kathyate / yatretyabhidheye / sādhyaṃ anityatvādi tasyābhāve hetoḥ kṛtakatvādeḥ / kim? / abhāva eva kathyate pratipādyate vacanena / taccedamudāharaṇaṃ darśayati / yannityaṃ tadakṛtakaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathākāśamiti sugamam / āha / na saugatānāṃ nityaṃ nāma kiṃcidasti / tadabhāvāt kathaṃ vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta ityucyate? / nityaśabdenātranityatvasyābhāva ucyate / atreti prayoge dṛṣṭāntavākye vā / kiṃ nityaśabdena anityasvasyābhāva ucyate? / anityo na bhavatīti nityaḥ / akṛtakaśabdenāpi kṛtakatvasyābhāvaḥ ucyate / iti ca vartate / kṛtakau na bhavatītyakṛtakaḥ / na tu vastu sannityamakṛtakaṃ vāsti / atraivodāharaṇamāha / yathā bhāvābhāvo 'bhāvaḥ / yathetyaupamye / bhāvaḥ sattā tasyābhāvo bhāvābhāvaḥ / asāvabhāva ucyate / na tu bhāvādanyo 'bhāvo nāma vastusvarūpo 'sti evaṃ nityaśabdenātretyādi dārṣṭāntike 'pi bhāvitameva // uktāḥ pakṣādayaḥ //
body.translated_text: The word '<s>vā</s>' has the meaning of '<s>ca</s>' (and). And it is used in the sense of conjunction (<s>samuccaya</s>). The statement of the second characteristic [of the reason]: '[The reason] is excluded from the <s>vipakṣa</s> (heterologous instance).' [Objection:] Even a valid reason (<s>samyaghetu</s>) that is present in only a part of the <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologous instances) [is valid] — as [shown by] the word '<s>yameva</s>' (whichever), which has the function of illustration, and is therefore not faulty. And is this reason only a property of the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-subject) — but not a property of the <s>pakṣa</s> exclusively [i.e., it need not be unique to it]? [This is because] the restriction (<s>avadhāraṇa</s>) has as its result merely the exclusion of other [unwanted] connections. Just as [in the expression] '<s>Caitra</s> is indeed an archer' [which does not deny that others are archers]. And by this, the four types of unestablished [reasons] (<s>asiddha</s>) and the uncommon [reason] (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) are excluded. Likewise, let the exclusion of other connections [in the second characteristic] also be fruitful, as in '<s>Pārtha</s> alone is the archer.' And by this, nine <s>hetvābhāsa</s>s (pseudo-reasons) — the common (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) and so on — are also excluded. [Objection:] If [the reason] exists only in the <s>sapakṣa</s>, then, since by exclusion from that [sapakṣa] there would be absence in the <s>pakṣa</s> as well, the status of being a property [of the pakṣa] would not be established. [Reply:] No, because the restriction [of the second characteristic regarding the sapakṣa] is not [yet] ascertained [at the time the first characteristic is established]; [whereas] the <s>pakṣadharmatva</s> (being a property of the thesis-subject) has [already] been ascertained. [Objection:] If so, '<s>vipakṣe nāsti eva</s>' — what is the purpose of this third restriction [regarding absence from the heterologous instance]? It is replied: for the purpose of demonstrating [proper] application [of the reason]. And it has been said: 'Even though a single characteristic — either of <s>anvaya</s> (positive correlation) or of <s>vyatireka</s> (negative correlation) — has been stated, how could it not imply the other?' Much remains to be said on this, but it is not said here, for fear of expanding the text. This [much] can be grasped by one's own intelligence. In '<s>anityādau hetu</s>' (the reason [is stated] in [proving] impermanence and so on), the word '<s>ādi</s>' (and so on) includes [qualities such as] suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>) and the like. Thus the <s>hetu</s> (reason) has been stated. Now, intending to state the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example), he says: 'The <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>' and so forth. '<s>Dṛṣṭānta</s>' means: 'that which leads one to the conclusion (<s>anta</s>) of a seen (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>) meaning' — the meaning is: in a dispute, it leads to a settled understanding of what has [already] been apprehended by a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge). And it is of two kinds (<s>dvividha</s>) — that which has two varieties. And he shows [these]: 'by similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) and by dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>).' 'A similar property' — that which has a similar property is '<s>sadharmā</s>'; the state of being a <s>sadharmā</s> is <s>sādharmya</s>; 'by that' [means: by similarity]. 'A dissimilar property' — that which has a dissimilar property is '<s>vidharmā</s>'; the state of being a <s>vidharmā</s> is <s>vaidharmya</s>; 'by that' [means: by dissimilarity]. The word '<s>ca</s>' is for conjunction. 'Therein, first by similarity' — the word '<s>tāvat</s>' is for [indicating] sequence. Regarding 'wherever' (<s>yatra</s>): the presence of the stated reason of stated definition in the <s>sapakṣa</s> alone is made known. The <s>sapakṣa</s> has the stated definition; and 'presence' means existence, being present — this is made known, communicated by means of a statement. And this [example by similarity] is: 'Whatever is produced is impermanent, like a pot and so on' — this is easy [to understand]. By this, the semblance of an example by similarity [is implicitly excluded]. 'By dissimilarity also' — 'wherever in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> (property to be proved), the absence of the <s>hetu</s> (reason) alone is stated.' Regarding 'wherever': in the subject under discussion. '<s>Sādhya</s>' means impermanence and the like; in its absence, [there is] the absence of the <s>hetu</s>, [namely] 'being produced' and the like. What [about it]? 'Absence alone is stated' — is communicated by means of a statement. And he shows this illustration: 'Whatever is permanent is unproduced, as observed, for example, like space' — this is easy [to understand]. [Objection:] For the Buddhists (<s>Saugatās</s>), there is nothing whatsoever that is permanent. In the absence of that, how can there be an example by dissimilarity? It is replied: By the word 'permanent' (<s>nitya</s>), the absence of impermanence is what is stated here — that is, in the application or in the example-statement. [Question:] Is it that the word 'permanent' denotes the absence of impermanence? [Reply:] That which 'is not impermanent' is permanent (<s>nitya</s>). By the word 'unproduced' (<s>akṛtaka</s>) also, the absence of being-produced is stated — and 'it continues' [i.e., the same analysis applies]. That which 'is not produced' is unproduced. But there is no real entity that is permanent or unproduced. Here itself he gives an illustration: 'Just as the absence of existence (<s>bhāva</s>) is absence (<s>abhāva</s>).' '<s>Yathā</s>' is for comparison. <s>Bhāva</s> means 'existence' or 'being'; its absence is '<s>bhāvābhāva</s>.' That is what is called '<s>abhāva</s>' (absence). But there is no real entity (<s>vastusvarūpa</s>) called '<s>abhāva</s>' that is different from <s>bhāva</s> (existence). Thus, with the word 'permanent' here and so on, the same has been established in the illustrative [example] as well. Thus the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) and the rest have been stated.

body.text: saha pakṣeṇa viṣayabhūtena hetudṛṣṭāntā ityarthaḥ / eṣāṃ vacanāni / eṣāmiti pakṣopalakṣitānāṃ hetudṛṣṭāntānām / vacanāni ye vācakāḥ śabdāḥ / kim? / parapratyāyanakāle prāsnikapratyāyanakāle sādhanam / yathā prayogato darśayati / yathā anityaḥ śabdaḥ iti pakṣavacanam / kṛtakatvāditi pakṣadharmavacanam / yat kṛtakaṃ tadanityaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathā ghaṭādiriti sapakṣānugamavacanam / yannityaṃ tadakṛtakaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathākāśamiti vyatirekavacanam / iti nigadasiddham / yāvat etānyeva trayo 'vayavā ityucyante / etānyeva pakṣahetudṛṣṭāntānāṃ vacanāni / traya iti saṃkhyā / avayavā ityucyante / pūrvācāryāṇāṃ saṃjñāntarametat / yathoktaṃ sādhanamavayavāḥ //
body.translated_text: The reason (<s>hetu</s>) and examples (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>), together with the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) which is the subject — their statements — this is the meaning. 'Of these' (<s>eṣām</s>) means: of the reason and examples, indicated by the thesis. 'Statements' (<s>vacanāni</s>) means: the words that express [them]. What? At the time of convincing another — at the time of convincing the examiner — [these constitute] the proof (<s>sādhana</s>). He illustrates this by way of a formal argument (<s>prayoga</s>): Thus, 'Sound is impermanent' is the thesis-statement; 'because it is produced' is the thesis-property-statement; 'whatever is produced is seen to be impermanent, like a pot and so on' is the statement of positive concomitance (<s>sapakṣānugama</s>); 'whatever is permanent is seen to be unproduced, like space' is the statement of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>). Thus it is established by the running text. That is to say, these alone are called 'the three members' (<s>avayava</s>). These very statements of thesis, reason, and example — three in number — are called 'members.' This is an alternative technical term of the earlier masters. As stated: 'The proof is the members.'

body.text: uktaṃ sādhanam / adhunā tadābhāsa ucyate / tatrāpi pakṣādivacanāni sādhanamiti pakṣasyopalakṣaṇatvātprathamaṃ pakṣa uktaḥ / ihāpi pakṣābhāsa evocyate sādhayitumityadi / sādhayitumiṣṭo 'pi pakṣādiviruddhaḥ pakṣābhāsaḥ / sisādhayiṣayā vāñchitaḥ apiśabdātprasiddho dharmītyādi tadanyalakṣaṇayukto 'pi / kim? / pratyakṣādiviruddhaḥ / virudhyate sa viruddhaḥ / pratyakṣādayo vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇāstairviruddho nirākṛtaḥ pratyakṣādiviruddhaḥ / kim? / pakṣābhāsaḥ / tasyātroktalakṣaṇaḥ pakṣaḥ ābhāsanamābhāsaḥ ākāramātram / pakṣasyevābhāso yasyāsau pakṣābhāsaḥ pakṣākāramātram / na tu samyak pakṣa ityarthaḥ / tadyathetyudāharaṇopanyāsārthaḥ / pratyakṣaviruddha ityādi / pratyakṣaṃ vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇam / iha punaḥ pratyakṣaśabdena tatparicchinno dharmaḥ parigṛhyate śālikuḍavanyāyāt / tataśca prasiddharmadharmaśabdalopāt pratyakṣaprasiddhadharmaviruddhaḥ pratyakṣaviruddhaḥ / evamanumānaviruddhaḥ āgamalokasvavacanaviruddhāśceti bhāvanīyamiti /
body.translated_text: Proof (<s>sādhana</s>) has been stated. Now its semblance (<s>ābhāsa</s>) is stated. Therein, since in the [statement] 'the statements of thesis and the rest constitute the proof,' the thesis has an indicative function, the thesis is stated first. Here too, only the thesis-semblance (<s>pakṣābhāsa</s>) is stated: 'That which is desired to be established...' and so on. 'A thesis-semblance is that which, though desired to be established, is contradicted by perception and the like.' 'Desired to be established' means: wished for with the intention to prove; the word 'api' [implies] also being well-known — [i.e., a <s>dharmin</s> that] also possesses the other characteristics stated above. What? [It is] 'contradicted by perception and the like.' That which is contradicted is <s>viruddha</s> (contradicted). Perception and the rest, having the definition to be stated — [the thesis that is] contradicted, i.e., refuted, by those — [that is] 'contradicted by perception and the like.' What? A thesis-semblance (<s>pakṣābhāsa</s>). Here, 'thesis' (<s>pakṣa</s>) has the definition stated above; 'semblance' (<s>ābhāsa</s>) is 'shining forth' — [meaning] mere appearance. That which has the mere appearance of a thesis — that is a thesis-semblance, i.e., a mere thesis-form, not a valid thesis — that is the meaning. The word 'that is to say' (<s>tadyathā</s>) is for the purpose of presenting examples. 'Contradicted by perception' and so on: perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) has the definition to be stated; but here, by the word 'perception,' the property determined by it is grasped, according to the principle of the 'rice-grain ladle.' Therefore, with the elision of the words 'well-known' and 'property,' 'contradicted by the property well-known through perception' is [what is meant by] 'contradicted by perception.' Similarly, 'contradicted by inference,' 'contradicted by scripture, common knowledge, and one's own statement' — these should be understood accordingly.

body.text: aprasiddhiviśeṣaṇādiśabdārthamudāharaṇanirūpaṇāyāmeva vakṣyāmaḥ / sāṃpratamudāharaṇāni darśayati / tatra pratyakṣaviruddhaḥ ityuddeśaḥ / yathā aśrāvaṇaḥ śabdaḥ ityudāharaṇam / atra śabdo dharmī / aśrāvaṇatvaṃ sādhyadharmaḥ / ayaṃ ca sādhyamānastatraiva dharmiṇi pratyakṣaprasiddhena śrāvaṇatvena virudhyate iti pratyakṣaviruddhaḥ / āha / śrāvaṇatvaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇatvātpratyakṣagamyameva na bhavati kathaṃ pratyakṣaprasiddhadharmaviruddhaḥ? iti / atrocyate / bhāvapratyayena svarūpamātrābhidhānātsāmānyalakṣaṇatvānupapatteradoṣa iti / atra ca bahu vaktavyaṃ tattu nocyate / akṣaragamanikāmāphalatvātprayāsasya // anumānaviruddho yathā / nityo ghaṭa iti / atra ghaṭo dharmī / nityatvaṃ sādhyadharmaḥ / sa cānumānaprasiddhenānityatvena tatraiva dharmiṇi bādhyate / anumānaṃ cedam / anityo ghaṭaḥ kāraṇādhīnātmalābhatvāt pradipavat // āgamaviruddho yathā / vaiśeṣikasya nityaḥ śabda iti sādhayataḥ / vaiśeṣiko 'hamityevaṃ pakṣaparigrahaṃ kṛtvā yadā śabdasya nityatvaṃ pratijānite tadāgamavirūddhaḥ / yatastasyāgame śabdasyānityatvaṃ prasiddham / uktaṃ ca buddhimatpūrvā vākyakṛtirvede tadvacanādāmnāyasya prāmāṇyamityādi // lokaviruddho yathā / śuci naraśiraḥkapālaṃ prāṇyaṅgatvāt śaṅkhaśuktivat iti / atra naraśiraḥkapālaṃ dharmitvenopādayite / śucitvaṃ sādhyadharmaḥ / sa ca sādhyamānastatraiva dharmiṇi lokaprasiddhaśucitvena nirākriyata iti / āha / iha hetudṛṣṭāntopādānaṃ kimarthamucyate? / lokasthiterbalīyastvakhyāpanārtham / nānumānenāpi lokaprasiddhirbādhyata ityarthaḥ // svavacanaviruddho yathā / mātā me vandhyā iti / iha ca mātā sādhyadharmitvenopāttā / vandhyeti ca sādhyadharmaḥ / sa ca sādhyamānastatraiva dharmiṇi svavacanaprasiddhena mātṛtvena viruddhyate / virodhaśca mātṛśabdena prasavadharmiṇī vanitocyate vandhyāśabdena tadviparītā / tataśca yadi mātā kathaṃ vandhyā? vandhyā cetkathaṃ māteti? // tathā aprasiddhaviśeṣaṇo yathā / bauddhasya sāṃkhyaṃ prati vināśī śabde iti / na prasiddhamaprasiddham / viśiṣyate aneneti viśeṣaṇaṃ sādhyadharmalakṣaṇam / tataścāprasiddhaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ yasmin sa tathāvidhaḥ / evaṃ śeṣepyakṣaragamanikā kāryeti / atra ca śabda iti nirdeśaḥ / vināśīti sādhyadharmaḥ / ayaṃ ca bauddhasya sāṃkhyaṃ prati aprasiddhiviśeṣaṇaḥ / na hi tasya siddhānte kiṃcidvinaśvaramasti / yata uktam- tadetatrailokyaṃ vyakterapaiti nityatvapratiṣedhāt / apetamapyasti vināśapratiṣedhādityādi [yāgasūtra- 3, 13 vyāsabhāṣya] / āha / yadyevaṃ na kaścitpakṣābhāso nāmāsti / tathāhi- vipratipattau iṣṭārthasiddhye 'numānaprayogaḥ / vipratipattireva caitaddoṣakartrīti kṛto 'numānam / atrocyate / na vipratipattimātraṃ taddoṣakartṛ yuktiviruddhatvāt / tathāhi- upapattibhirdṛṣṭāntasādhane kṛte 'numānaprayogaḥ iṣṭārthasiddhaye bhavati / nānyathā / punaḥ sādhanāpekṣatvāt / ato dṛṣṭāntaṃ prasādhya prayogaḥ kartavya iti / aprasādhite tu pakṣābhāsaḥ / iti kṛta prasaṅgena // tathā aprasiddhaviśeṣyo yathā sāṃkhyasya bauddhaṃ prati cetana ātmeti / tatra viśeṣyo dharmītyanarthāntaram / iha cātmā dharmī / cetanatvaṃ sādhyadharmaḥ / iti pakṣaḥ sāṃkhyasya bauddhaṃ prati aprasiddhaviśeṣyaḥ / ātmano 'prasiddhatvāt / sarve dharmā nirātmāna ityabhyupagamāt /
body.translated_text: We shall explain the meaning of the words 'having an unestablished qualifier' and so on precisely when examining the examples. For now, he shows the examples. Therein, 'contradicted by perception' (<s>pratyakṣaviruddha</s>) is the summary statement. 'For example: sound is inaudible' is the illustration. Here, sound is the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>); inaudibility is the property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharma</s>). And this [property], while being proved, is contradicted in that very property-bearer by audibility, which is well-known through perception — hence it is 'contradicted by perception.' [Objection:] He says — audibility, being a general characteristic, is not itself accessible to perception; how then is it 'contradicted by a property well-known through perception'? [Reply:] To this it is said — since the term with the existential suffix (<s>bhāvapratyaya</s>) denotes only the essential nature [of the thing], the [objection based on] being a general characteristic is untenable — hence there is no fault. And here much could be said, but it is not stated, because the effort of letter-by-letter analysis would be fruitless. 'Contradicted by inference' (<s>anumānaviruddha</s>), for example: 'the pot is eternal.' Here, the pot is the property-bearer; eternality is the property to be proved. And this is defeated in that very property-bearer by non-eternality, which is well-known through inference. And the inference is this: 'The pot is non-eternal, because its existence depends on causes — like a lamp.' 'Contradicted by scripture' (<s>āgamaviruddha</s>), for example: when a <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> tries to prove that 'sound is eternal' — having adopted the position 'I am a <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>,' when he asserts the eternality of sound, it is contradicted by scripture, because the non-eternality of sound is well-known in his own scripture. And it has been said: 'The composition of sentences in the <s>Veda</s> is preceded by intelligence; from that [divine] utterance, the authority of tradition [follows]' and so on. 'Contradicted by common experience' (<s>lokaviruddha</s>), for example: 'A human skull is pure, because it is a part of a living being — like a conch or oyster shell.' Here, the human skull is taken as the property-bearer; purity is the property to be proved. And this, while being proved, is refuted in that very property-bearer by its impurity, which is well-known in common experience. [Objection:] He says — why is the inclusion of reason and example stated here? [Reply:] For the purpose of making known that common experience is stronger [than inference]; the meaning is that even by inference, common knowledge cannot be overridden. 'Contradicted by one's own statement' (<s>svavacanaviruddha</s>), for example: 'My mother is barren.' Here, 'mother' is taken as the property-bearer of the property to be proved; 'barren' is the property to be proved. And this, while being proved, is contradicted in that very property-bearer by motherhood, which is well-known from one's own statement. The contradiction is this: by the word 'mother,' a woman possessing the property of having given birth is denoted; by the word 'barren,' the opposite. Therefore, if [she is] a mother, how can she be barren? And if barren, how can she be a mother? Likewise, 'having an unestablished qualifier' (<s>aprasiddhaviśeṣaṇa</s>), for example: of a Buddhist toward a <s>Sāṃkhya</s> [opponent]: 'Sound is destructible.' The qualifier is that which is not established [for the opponent] — the property to be proved, which is characterized as the distinguishing attribute. Therefore, one in whom there is an unestablished qualifier is of that kind. The letter-by-letter analysis of the rest should be done similarly. Here, 'sound' is the subject; 'destructible' is the property to be proved. And this is one with an unestablished qualifier for a Buddhist toward a <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, because in the latter's doctrine nothing whatsoever is destructible — since it has been said: 'This triple world departs from the manifest; [but this does] not [mean] negation of eternality. Even what has departed still exists; [this does] not [mean] negation of destruction' and so on [<s>Yogasūtra</s> 3.13, <s>Vyāsabhāṣya</s>]. [Objection:] He says — if this is so, there is no such thing as a pseudo-thesis (<s>pakṣābhāsa</s>). For [one might argue]: inference is employed for establishing the desired meaning when there is disagreement; and it is precisely this disagreement that produces the fault — hence inference is [always] possible. [Reply:] To this it is said — mere disagreement alone does not produce that fault, because it would be contrary to reason. For when the establishment of the example is accomplished through reasonings, the inferential procedure serves to establish the desired meaning — not otherwise, because it depends on [prior] establishment. Therefore, having first established the example, the inferential procedure should be carried out. But when [the example] has not been established, it is a pseudo-thesis. Thus [this has been stated] as a digression. Likewise, 'having an unestablished qualificand' (<s>aprasiddhaviśeṣya</s>), for example: of a <s>Sāṃkhya</s> toward a Buddhist: 'The self (<s>ātman</s>) is conscious.' Here, the qualificand and the property-bearer are synonymous. Here, the <s>ātman</s> is the property-bearer; consciousness is the property to be proved. Thus the thesis is one with an unestablished qualificand for a <s>Sāṃkhya</s> toward a Buddhist, because the <s>ātman</s> is not established [for the Buddhist] — since they accept that 'all <s>dharmas</s> are without self (<s>nirātman</s>).'

body.text: ākṣepaparihārau pūrvavat // tathā aprasiddhobhayo yathā / vaiśeṣikasya bauddhaṃ prati sukhādisamavāyikāraṇamātmā iti / ubhayaṃ dharmadharmiṇau / tatrātmā dharmī / sukhādisamavāyikāraṇatvaṃ sādhyadharmaḥ / vaiśeṣikasya hi kāraṇatrayātkāryaṃ bhavati / tadyathā- samavāyikāraṇāt asamavāyikāraṇāt nimittakāraṇācca / tathāhi- tantavaḥ paṭasya samacāyikāraṇaṃ tantusaṃyogo 'samavāyikāraṇaṃ turīvemādayastu nimittakāraṇam / itthamātmā sukhaduḥkhecchādīnāṃ samavāyikāraṇam / ātmamanaḥsaṃyogo 'samavāyikāraṇam / srakcandanādayo nimittakāraṇam / ityevaṃ vaiśeṣikasya bauddhaṃ prati aprasiddhobhayaḥ / na tasyātmā viśeṣyaḥ siddho nāpi samavāyikāraṇaṃ viśeṣaṇam / sāmagryā eva janakatvābhyupagamāt / ākṣepaparihārau pūrvavat // tathā prasiddhasaṃbandho yathā śrāvaṇaḥ śabda iti / prasiddho vādiprativādinoravipratipattyā sthitaḥ saṃbandho dharmadharmilakṣaṇo yasmin sa tathāvidhaḥ / iha śabdo dharmī śrāvaṇatvaṃ sādhyadharmaḥ / ubhayaṃ caitat vādiprativādinoḥ prasiddham / eṣāṃ vacanāni ityādi / eṣāmiti navānāmapi paramārśaḥ / vacanāni / pratijñādoṣā iti saṃbandhaḥ kāraṇamāha / dharmasvarūpanirākaraṇamukhena pañcānāmādyānām / svaṃ ca tadrūpaṃ ca svarūpamityarthaḥ / nirākriyate 'neneti nirākarotīti vā nirākaraṇam / pratiṣedhanamityarthaḥ / dharmasvarūpasya nirākaraṇaṃ tattathā mukhamiva mukhaṃ dvāramiti bhāvaḥ / dharmasvarūpanirākaraṇameva mukhaṃ tena dharmasvarūpanirākaraṇamukhena dharmayāthātmyapratiṣedhadvāreṇetyarthaḥ / pratiṣidhyate cāśrāvaṇaḥ śabdaḥ / ityevamādiṣu pañcasu pratyakṣādiprasiddhaṃ dharmayāthātmyamiti bhāvanā / tathā pratipādanāsaṃbhavatastrayāṇām / tatra pratipādyate 'nena pratipādayatīti vā pratipādanam / paramapratyāyanamiti hṛdayam / tasyāsaṃbhavaḥ pratipādanāsaṃbhavaḥ tasmāt pratipādanāsaṃbhavataḥ / na ca dṛṣṭāntādyapratipattau pratipādanaṃ saṃbhavati / tathā sādhanavaiphalyataścaikasya / viphalasya bhāvo vaiphalyaṃ sādhanasya vaiphalyaṃ sādhanavaiphalyaṃ tasmātsādhanavaiphalyataḥ / ca samuccaye / tataśca eṣāṃ vacanāni / pratijñādoṣāḥ / pratijñāpakṣa ityanarthāntaram / doṣābhāsa iti ca tulyam / ityabhihitāḥ pakṣābhāsāḥ //
body.translated_text: The objection and its resolution are as before. Similarly, [an example of a thesis that is] 'unestablished for both' (<s>aprasiddhobhaya</s>): as when the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>, [arguing] against the Buddhist, [proposes:] 'The self (<s>ātman</s>) is the co-inherent cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>) of pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) etc.' Both [here refers to] the property and the property-bearer (<s>dharma</s> and <s>dharmin</s>). There, the self is the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>); 'being the co-inherent cause of pleasure etc.' is the property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharma</s>). For the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>, an effect arises from three [types of] causes: namely, the co-inherent cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>), the non-co-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>), and the efficient cause (<s>nimittakāraṇa</s>). For example: the threads are the co-inherent cause of a cloth; the conjunction of the threads is the non-co-inherent cause; and the shuttle, loom, and such are the...

body.text: sāṃprataṃ hetvābhāsānabhidhitsurāha / asiddhānaikāntikaviruddhā hetvābhāsāḥ / asiddhaśca anaikāntikaśca viruddhaśca asiddhānaikāntikaviruddhāḥ / hetuvadābhāsante iti hetvābhāsāḥ / yathoddeśaṃ nirdeśa iti nyāyamaṅgīkṛtyāsiddhapratipipādayiṣayāha / tatrāsiddhaścatuḥprakāraḥ / tatra eṣu asiddhādiṣu / asiddhaḥ sidhyati sa siddhaḥ pratītaḥ na siddhaḥ asiddhaḥ apratītaḥ / catuḥprakāraścaturbhedaḥ / prakārāndarśayati / tadyathā / ubhayāsiddha ityādi / tadyatheti pūrvavat / ubhayorvādiprativādinoḥ asiddha ubhayāsiddhaḥ // anyatarasya vādinaḥ prativādino vā asiddha anyatarāsiddhaḥ // saṃdihyate sa saṃdigdhaḥ / saṃdigdhatvādevāsiddhaḥ saṃdigdhasiddhaḥ // āśrayo dharmī so 'siddho yasyāsau āśrayāsiddhaḥ / ca samuccaye / itiśabdaḥ parisamāptyarthaḥ // idānīmudāharaṇānyāha / tatra śabdānityatve ityādi / tatreti pūrvavat / śabdānityatve sādhye anityaḥ śabdaḥ ityetasmin cākṣuṣatvāditi /
body.translated_text: Now, intending to expound the pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>), [the text] states: 'The unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), the inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), and the contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>) are the pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>).' Unestablished and inconclusive and contradictory [are together called] 'the unestablished, inconclusive, and contradictory.' [They are called] <s>hetvābhāsa</s> because they merely appear like a [valid] reason (<s>hetu</s>). Accepting the principle that 'the exposition should follow the order of the enumeration,' and wishing to expound the 'unestablished,' [the text] states: 'Therein, the unestablished is of four kinds.' 'Therein' — among these, namely the unestablished etc. The 'unestablished' (<s>asiddha</s>) [means:] that which is established is <s>siddha</s>, i.e. recognized; that which is not established is <s>asiddha</s>, i.e. unrecognized. 'Of four kinds' means of four varieties...

body.text: cakṣurindriyagrāhyaścākṣuṣastadbhāvaścākṣuṣatvam / tasmādityayaṃ heturubhayāsiddhaḥ / tathāhi- cākṣuṣatvaṃ na vādinaḥ prasiddhaṃ nāpi prativādinaḥ / śrotrendriyagrāhyatvācchabdasya // kṛtakatvāditi śabdābhivyaktivādinaṃ prati anyatarāsiddhaḥ / śabdanityatve sādhye iti / vartate kṛtakatvādityayaṃ hetuḥ śabdābhivyaktivādinaṃ mīmāṃsakaṃ kāpilaṃ vā pratyanyatarāsiddhaḥ / tathāhi- na tasya tālvoṣṭhapuṭādibhiḥ kriyate śabdaḥ kiṃtvabhivyajyata iti // tathā bāṣpādibhāvenetyādi / bāṣpo jalādiprabhavaḥ sa ādiryasya reṇuvartyādeḥ sa bāṣpādistasya bhāvaḥ sattā tena bāṣpādibhāvena / saṃdihyamānaḥ kimayaṃ dhūma uta bāṣpa uta reṇuvartiriti saṃdehamāpadyamānaḥ / bhūtasaṃghātaḥ sūkṣmaḥ kṣityādisamūhaḥ / kim? / agneḥ siddhiragnisiddhistasyāmagnisiddhau / agniratra thūmāditi upadiśyamānaḥ procyamānaḥ saṃdigdhāsiddhaḥ / niścito hi dhūmo dhūmatvena hutavahaṃ gamayati nāniścita iti / tathā dravyamākāśamityādi / ākāśa iti dharminirdeśaḥ / dravyamiti sādhyo dharmaḥ / guṇāścāsya ṣaṭ / tadyathā / saṃkhyā parimāṇaṃ pṛthaktvaṃ saṃyogo vibhāgaḥ śabdeśceti //
body.translated_text: That which is graspable by the eye-organ is 'visual' (<s>cākṣuṣa</s>); its state is 'visuality' (<s>cākṣuṣatva</s>). Therefore — this reason is 'unestablished for both parties' (<s>ubhayāsiddha</s>). For indeed, 'visuality' is not established for the proponent, nor for the opponent — because sound is graspable by the ear-organ. 'Because of being produced' (<s>kṛtakatvāt</s>) — [this reason is] 'unestablished for one party' (<s>anyatarāsiddha</s>) against the advocate of the manifestation [theory] of sound. 'When the permanence of sound is to be proved' — it continues. The reason 'because of being produced' is 'unestablished for one party' against the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> or the <s>Kāpila</s> (Sāṃkhya) who advocates that sound is manifested. For indeed, [according to them,] sound is not produced by the palate, lips, cheeks, and the like, but rather [merely] manifested. Likewise, 'by the state of being steam etc.' and so on: steam (<s>bāṣpa</s>) arises from water and the like; '<s>bāṣpādi</s>' means 'that which has steam as its beginning,' i.e., steam, dust-motes, and the like; 'by the state of being' (<s>bhāva</s>) means 'by the existence' of that. '[The reason which is] doubted' — [wondering:] 'Is this smoke, or steam, or a dust-mote?' — the one who is falling into doubt. 'A subtle aggregate of elements (<s>bhūtasaṃghāta</s>)' — a collection of earth and the like. What? '[For] the establishment of fire' — and in that [context of] fire-establishment, the [reason] 'there is fire here based on smoke and so on,' being taught, being stated, is '<s>saṃdigdhāsiddha</s>' (doubtfully unestablished). For only smoke that is certain as smoke leads one to [know] fire, not uncertain [smoke]. Likewise, 'substance [and] space' and so on: 'space' is the statement of the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer); 'substance' is the property to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>). And its qualities are six, namely: number, measure, separateness, conjunction, disjunction, and sound.

body.text: tatra guṇānāmāśrayaḥ guṇāśrayastadbhāvastattvaṃ tasmāt guṇāśrayatvāditi / ayaṃ heturākāśāsattvavādinaṃ bauddhaṃ pratyāśrayāsiddhaḥ / dharmiṇa evāsiddhatvāt / tathā ca tasyāyaṃ siddhāntaḥ / pañca imāni bhikṣavaḥ saṃjñāmātraṃ saṃvṛtimātraṃ pratijñāmātraṃ vyavahāramātraṃ kalpanāmātram / katamāni pañca / atītaḥ addhā anāgataḥ addhā pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ ākāśaṃ pugdala iti / nanu cānyo 'pyasti asiddhaḥ sa ca dvidhā / pratijñārthaikadeśāsiddhaḥ / yathā anityaḥ śabdo 'nityatvāt / avyāpakāsiddhaśceti / yathā sacetanāstaravaḥ svāpāt / sa kasmānnoktaḥ / ācārya āha / antarbhāvāt / kva punarantarbhāva iti cait ubhayāsiddhe / tasmādadoṣaḥ / āha / yadyevamasiddhabhedadvayamevāstu ubhayāsiddho 'nyatarāsiddhaśceti / śeṣadvayasyātraivāntarbhāvāt / tathā cānyairapyuktam-
body.translated_text: Therein, 'the substrate of qualities' is 'quality-substrate' (<s>guṇāśraya</s>); its state is that-ness (<s>tattva</s>); therefore, 'because of being a substrate of qualities' (<s>guṇāśrayatvāt</s>). This reason is '<s>āśrayāsiddha</s>' (unestablished as to the substrate) against the Buddhist who maintains the non-existence of space — because the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) itself is unestablished [for him]. And thus his doctrinal position is: 'These five, O monks, are mere designations, mere conventions, mere assertions, mere practical usages, mere conceptual constructions. Which five? Past time, future time, analytical cessation (<s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>), space (<s>ākāśa</s>), and the individual (<s>pudgala</s>).' Now, there is also another [type of] 'unestablished' [reason], and it is twofold: 'unestablished as to a part of the thesis-meaning' — for example, 'sound is impermanent, because of impermanence'; and 'unestablished as non-pervasive' — for example, 'trees are sentient, because of sleep.' Why was that not stated [by the author]? The <s>Ācārya</s> says: because of subsumption. Where then does the subsumption [occur]? Under 'unestablished for both parties.' Therefore, [there is] no fault. He says: If so, let there be only two divisions of 'unestablished' — 'unestablished for both parties' and 'unestablished for one party' — since the other two are subsumed under these very [two]. And others also have said —

body.text: asiddhabhedau dvāveva dvayoranyatarasya vā //
body.translated_text: 'The divisions of the unestablished [reason] are just two: [unestablished] for both or for either one.'

body.text: ityādi / naitadevam / dharmyasiddhihetusaṃdehopādhidvāreṇa bhedaviśeṣasya siddheḥ / vineyavyutpattiphalatvācca śastrārambhasya / paryāptaṃ vistareṇokto 'siddhaḥ // sāṃpratam anaikāntikaḥ ucyate / sa ca ṣaṭprakāraḥ ṣaḍvidhaḥ / ekānte bhava aikāntikaḥ / na aikāntikau 'naikāntikaḥ / ṣaṭ prakārā asyeti ṣaṭprakāraḥ ṣaḍ vidhaityarthaḥ // bhedānevāha / sādhāraṇa ityādi / anvartham / ityudāharaṇameva vakṣyāmaḥ / tatra sādhāraṇaḥ prabheyatvānnitya iti / tatreti pūrvavat / dvayorbahūnāṃ vā yaḥ sāmānyaḥ sa sādhāraṇaḥ / pramīyate iti prameyo jñeya ityarthaḥ tadbhāvaḥ prameyatvaṃ tasmātprameyatvāt pramāṇaparicchedyatvāt / nitya ityatra śabdākhyo dharmī gamyate / idaṃ ca sapakṣetarākāśaghaṭādibhāvena sādhāraṇatvāt saṃśayanimittamiti / āha ca / taddhi nityānityetyādi / tat prameyatvaṃ dharmaḥ / hi rūpapradarśane / nityaścānityaśca nityānityau nityānityau ca tau pakṣau ca nityānityapakṣau / tayornityānityapakṣayorityarthaḥ / kim? / sādhāraṇatvāt tulyavṛttitvādanaikāntikam / prayoga eva darśayati / kiṃ ghaṭavat prameyatvādanityaḥ śabdaḥ āhosvidākāśavat prameyatvānnitya iti prakaṭārthaṃ darśayati / aho nāyaṃ saṃśayahetuḥ / etatprayogamantareṇa prāgeva saṃśayasya bhāvāt / tadbhāvabhāvitvānupapatteḥ / uktaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: ...and so forth.
