This is not so, because the specific distinction [within the <s>asiddha</s> category] is established through the doors of doubt regarding the <s>dharmin</s>-establishment, the reason, and the adventitious condition (<s>upādhi</s>); and because the undertaking of the <s>śāstra</s> has as its fruit the instruction of the trainee. The 'unestablished' (<s>asiddha</s>) has been fully stated in detail. Now the 'inconclusive' (<s>anaikāntika</s>) is discussed. And it is of six kinds — sixfold. That which occurs in one direction (<s>ekānta</s>) is <s>aikāntika</s> (conclusive); that which is not conclusive is <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive). 'Of six kinds' means having six varieties — sixfold, that is the meaning. [The text] states the varieties themselves: '<s>sādhāraṇa</s>' (common) and so forth. The [designation] follows [its] meaning. Examples will now be stated...

children.translated_text: And the varieties of the inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) are not at all a cause of doubt —
since, when doubt exists and the reason is stated, there is no distinction regarding [the reason's] existence [in both <s>sapakṣa</s> and <s>vipakṣa</s>].

body.text: ityādi / naitadevam / saṃśayasyāvivakṣitatvāt / tamantareṇāpi prayogopapatteśca / kriyate ca viparyastamatiprabhṛtipratipattyarthamapi prayogaḥ / tatrāpi saṃśayahetutvādanaikāntikāmiti // asādhāraṇaḥ śrāvaṇatvānnitya ityādi / sādhāraṇavilakṣaṇaḥ asādhāraṇaḥ asāmānyaḥ pakṣadharmaḥ san sapakṣavipakṣābhyāṃ vyāvṛtta ityarthaḥ / udāharaṇamāha / śrāvaṇatvānnitya iti / śravaṇendriyagrāhyaḥ śrāvaṇastadbhāvaḥ śrāvaṇatvaṃ tasmāt / nityaḥ avināśī / śabda iti gamyate / tatredaṃ śrāvaṇatvaṃ svadharmiṇaṃ vihāya na sapakṣe ākāśādau nāpi vipakṣe ghaṭādau vartata iti saṃśayanimittam / ata evāha / taddhītyādi / tat śrāvaṇatvam / hi rūpapradarśane nityānityapakṣābhyāṃ vyāvṛttatvāt / saṃśayaheturiti yogaḥ / anyatra vartiṣyata itīdamapi nirākurvannāha / nityānityavinirmuktasya cānyasya cāsaṃbhavāt / yadasti tena nityena vā bhavitavyamanityena vā nānyathā / virodhādatiprasaṃgācca / ataḥ saṃśayahetuḥ saṃśayakāraṇam / kathamityāha / kiṃbhūtasyetyādi / kiṃprakārasya kiṃ nityasyāhosvidanityasyāsyeti / prastutasya śabdasya śrāvaṇatvamityetaduktaṃ bhavati / yadi tadanyatra nitye vānitye vopalabdhaṃ bhavati tatastabdalenetaratrāpi niścayo yujyate nānyathā / viparyakalpanāyā apyanyanivāritaprasaratvāt / ityatra bahu vaktavyam / alaṃ prasaṅgena / ākṣepaparihārau pūrvavat / evaṃ śeṣeṣvapi bhāvanīyamiti // sapakṣaikadeśavṛttirityādi / samānaḥ pakṣaḥ sapakṣaḥ tasyaikadeśaḥ sapakṣaikadeśaḥ tasminvṛttirasyeti sapakṣaikadeśavṛttiḥ / tathā visadṛśaḥ pakṣo vipakṣastaṃ vyāptuṃ śīlamasyeti vipakṣavyāpī / udāharaṇamāha / yathā / aprayatnānantarīyakaḥ śabdo nityatvāditi / śabdo dharmī / aprayatnānantarīyakatvaṃ sādhyo dharmaḥ / anityatvāditi hetuḥ / tatra aprayatnānantarīyakaḥ pakṣaḥ / aprayatnānantarīyako 'rthaḥ / asya sādhyavidyudākāśādipadārthasaṃghātaḥ kim? / sapakṣaḥ / tatraikadeśe vidyudādau vartate 'nityatvaṃ nākāśādau / nityatvāttasya / tathā aprayatnānantarīyakaḥ pakṣo 'sya ghaṭādirvipakṣaḥ / tatra sarvatra ghaṭādau vidyate 'nityatvam / prayatnāntarīyakasyānityatvāt / yasmādevaṃ tasmādetadapi anityatvaṃ vidyudghatasādharmyeṇa vidyudghatulyatayānikāntikam / bhāvanikāmāha / kiṃ ghaṭavat anityatvāt prayatnānantarīyakaḥ / śabdaḥ āhosvidvidyudādivadanityatvādaprayatnānantarīyaka iti /
body.translated_text: And so on. This is not so, because doubt is not intended [as the purpose of inference], and because the application [of inference] is justified even without it, and because inference is also employed for the purpose of producing understanding in those with reversed cognition and the like. Even there, because it [the reason] is a cause of doubt, it is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). [Next:] 'The uncommon [reason]: [sound is] permanent because of audibility (<s>śrāvaṇatva</s>),' and so on. The uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) [reason], unlike the common (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) [reason], is a property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) that is excluded from both the homologous instances (<s>sapakṣa</s>) and the heterologous instances (<s>vipakṣa</s>) — this is the meaning. He gives an example: '[Sound is] permanent because of audibility.' That which is graspable by the auditory sense-faculty is 'audible' (<s>śrāvaṇa</s>); its nature is audibility (<s>śrāvaṇatva</s>) — therefore [the inference is based on that]. 'Permanent' means 'indestructible.' 'Sound' is understood [as the subject]. Here, this audibility, apart from its own <s>dharmin</s> [i.e., sound], does not occur in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologous instance) such as space, nor in the <s>vipakṣa</s> (heterologous instance) such as a pot — and this is the ground for doubt. Hence he says: 'That, indeed,' and so on. 'That' means audibility. 'Indeed' is for the purpose of demonstrating the nature [of the reason]: because it is excluded from both the permanent and impermanent theses, the connection is that it is a cause of doubt. Refuting also [the idea] that it might occur elsewhere, he says: Because of the impossibility of any [instance] other than [what is] free from [both] permanent and impermanent [things]. Whatever exists must be either permanent or impermanent — not otherwise — because of [mutual] contradiction and because of over-extension. Therefore it is a cause of doubt, meaning a ground for uncertainty. How? He says: 'Of what sort?' and so on. 'Of what character?' — [the question is:] 'Is this [sound] permanent or impermanent?' — this is what has been stated regarding the sound under discussion, [i.e.,] its audibility. If that [audibility] were found elsewhere, in something permanent or in something impermanent, then from that indication a determination in the other [domain] too would be justified — not otherwise — because even a contrary supposition would have its scope unblocked by any other [consideration]. Much could be said on this point; but enough of this digression. The objection and its resolution are as before. The same should be understood regarding the remaining [types] as well. [Next:] 'Occurring in only part of the <s>sapakṣa</s>,' and so on. A 'similar thesis' (<s>sapakṣa</s>) is a thesis that is the same [in possessing the probandum]; 'one part of the <s>sapakṣa</s>' is <s>sapakṣaikadeśa</s>; 'occurring in that' is <s>sapakṣaikadeśavṛtti</s> (occurring in only part of the homologous instances). Likewise, a 'dissimilar thesis' (<s>vipakṣa</s>) is one that is different; 'whose habit is to pervade that' is <s>vipakṣavyāpī</s> (pervading the heterologous instances). He gives an example: 'Sound is not the immediate consequence of effort, because of permanence.' Sound is the <s>dharmin</s>; not being the immediate consequence of effort (<s>aprayatnānantarīyakatva</s>) is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum); 'because of permanence' is the <s>hetu</s> (reason). There, 'not being the immediate consequence of effort' is the thesis. 'Not being the immediate consequence of effort' is the meaning. Of this [thesis], the collection of entities such as lightning, space, and the like — what [are they]? — [They are] the <s>sapakṣa</s>. In only part of that [<s>sapakṣa</s>] — in lightning and the like — permanence occurs, but not in space and the like, because of their permanence. Likewise, 'not being the immediate consequence of effort' is the thesis, [and] of this, pots and the like are the <s>vipakṣa</s>. There, in all [instances] such as pots and the like, permanence is found — because what is the immediate consequence of effort is impermanent. Since this is so, therefore this permanence too, by reason of its similarity with both lightning and pots, being equally [present] in [both] lightning and pots, is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). Stating the import, he says: Is sound the immediate consequence of effort because of its impermanence — like a pot? Or is it not the immediate consequence of effort because of its impermanence — like lightning and the like?

body.text: prakaṭārtham // vipakṣaikadeśavṛtiḥ sapakṣavyāpī / samāsaḥ sukara eva / udāharaṇamāha / yathā prayatnānantarīyakaḥ śabdo 'nityatvāt / prayatnānantarīyakaḥ pakṣo 'sya ghaṭādiḥ sapakṣaḥ / tatra sarvatra ghaṭādau vidyate 'nityatvam / prayatnānantarīyakaḥ pakṣo 'sya vidyudākāśādirvipakṣaḥ / tatraikadeśe vidyudādau vidyate 'nityatvam / nākāśādau / tasmādetadapi vidyudghaṭasādharmyeṇa pūrvavadanaikāntikam iti sūtrārthaḥ / uktavaiparītyena svadhiyā bhāvanīyamiti // ubhayapakṣaikadeśavṛttiḥ / ubhayapakṣayoḥ sapakṣavipakṣayorekadeśavṛttirasyeti ubhayapakṣaikadeśavṛttiḥ / udāharaṇamāha / yathā nityaḥ śabdo 'mūrtatvāditi // nityaḥ pakṣo 'syākāśaparamāṇvādiḥ sapakṣaḥ / tatraikadeśa ākāśārdo vidyate 'mūrtatvaṃ na paramāṇvādau / anityaḥ pakṣo 'sya ghaṭasukhādirvipakṣaḥ / tatraikadeśe sukhādau vidyate 'mūrtatvaṃ na ghaṭādau / tasmādetadapi sukhākāśasādharmyeṇānaikāntikam / etadapi sūtraṃ nigadasiddham / tathā viruddhāvyabhicārī / adhikṛtahetvanumeyaviruddhārthasādhako viruddhaḥ / viruddhaṃ na vyabhicaratīti viruddhāvyabhicārī / upanyastaḥ san tathāvidhārthānirākṛteḥ pratiyoginaṃ na vyabhicaratīti bhāvaḥ / tataścānena pratiyogisādhyamapākṛtya hetuprayogaḥ kartavya ityetadāha / anye tu viruddhaścāsāvavyabhicārī ca viruddhāvyabhicārīti vyācakṣate / idaṃ punarayuktameva / virodhādanekāntavādāpatteśca / udāharaṇamāha / yathānityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvād ghaṭavat / nityaḥ śabdaḥ śrāvaṇatvāt śabdatvavat / ubhayoḥ saṃśayahetutvāt dvāvapyetāveko 'naikāntikaḥ samuditāveva / anityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvādghaṭavaditi vaiśeṣikeṇokte mīmāṃsaka āha / nityaḥ śabdaḥ śrāvaṇatvāt śabdatvavat / śabdatvaṃ hi nāma veṇuvīṇāmṛdaṅgapaṇavādibhedabhinneṣu sarvaśabdeṣu śabda ityabhinnābhidhānapratyayanibandhanaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣasaṃjñitaṃ nityamiti / ubhayoḥ saṃśayahetutvāditi / ekatra dharmiṇi ubhayoḥ kṛtakatvaśrāvaṇatvayoḥ saṃśayahetutvāt saṃdehahetutvā / tathā caikatra dharmiṇi kṛtakatvaśrāvaṇatvākhyau hetu saṃdehaṃ kurutaḥ kiṃ kṛtakatvādghaṭavadanityaḥ āhosvicchrāvaṇatvācchabdatvavannityaḥ iti / evaṃ saṃdehahetutve pratipādite paraścodayati kiṃ samastayoḥ saṃdehahetutvam uta vyastayoḥ /
body.translated_text: The meaning is self-evident. [The fifth type of inconclusive reason:] Present in a part of the <s>vipakṣa</s> (heterologous instance), pervading the entire <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologous instance). The compound analysis is easy to perform. He gives an example: 'Sound is that which immediately follows effort, because of impermanence.' 'That which immediately follows effort' is the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis); its <s>sapakṣa</s> is a pot and the like. In all of those — pots and so on — impermanence is present. 'That which immediately follows effort' is the <s>pakṣa</s>; its <s>vipakṣa</s> is lightning, space, and the like. In a part of that [<s>vipakṣa</s>] — in lightning and so forth — impermanence is present, but not in space and the like. Therefore, this too is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) by the similarity with lightning and pot, as before — this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>. [The remaining analysis] should be developed by one's own intelligence in reverse of what has been stated. [The sixth type:] Present in a part of both instances (<s>ubhayapakṣaikadeśavṛtti</s>) — that which is present in a part of both instances, namely the <s>sapakṣa</s> and the <s>vipakṣa</s>, is called 'present in a part of both instances.' He gives an example: 'Sound is permanent, because of incorporeality (<s>amūrtatva</s>).' 'Permanent' is the <s>pakṣa</s>; its <s>sapakṣa</s> is space, atoms, and the like. In a part of that — in space and the like — incorporeality is present, but not in atoms and the like. 'Impermanent' is the <s>pakṣa</s>; its <s>vipakṣa</s> is a pot, pleasure, and the like. In a part of that — in pleasure and the like — incorporeality is present, but not in a pot and the like. Therefore, this too is inconclusive by the similarity with pleasure and space. This <s>sūtra</s> too is established by the running text. Likewise, the <s>viruddhāvyabhicārin</s> (the counter-balanced): 'contradictory' (<s>viruddha</s>) means that which establishes a meaning contrary to what is to be inferred by the reason under discussion; '<s>viruddhāvyabhicārin</s>' means 'that which does not deviate from the contradictory' — the sense is: having been presented, since [the reason] does not refute such a [contradictory] meaning, it does not deviate from the counter-thesis. And therefore, [the text] says: one should first set aside the [opponent's] counter-thesis by means of this [reason] and then apply the reason. Others, however, explain it as: 'it is both contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>) and non-deviating (<s>avyabhicārin</s>), hence <s>viruddhāvyabhicārin</s>.' But this is indeed untenable, because of [internal] contradiction and the consequence of [embracing] the doctrine of indeterminacy. He gives an example: 'Sound is impermanent, because of being produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>), like a pot. Sound is permanent, because of being audible (<s>śrāvaṇatva</s>), like sound-universal (<s>śabdatva</s>).' Because both [reasons] cause doubt, these two together constitute a single inconclusive [reason]. When the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> states 'Sound is impermanent because of being produced, like a pot,' the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> replies: 'Sound is permanent because of being audible, like sound-universal.' For <s>śabdatva</s> (sound-universal) is the common-particular (<s>sāmānyaviśeṣa</s>) that is the basis of the identical designation and cognition 'sound' in all sounds differentiated by the varieties of flute, lute, drum, kettledrum, and so on — and it is permanent. 'Because both cause doubt' — because both 'being produced' and 'being audible,' [applied to] the single <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer), are causes of doubt. And thus, in a single property-bearer, the two reasons called 'being produced' and 'being audible' cause doubt: 'Is [sound] impermanent like a pot because of being produced, or is it permanent like sound-universal because of being audible?' When the fact of causing doubt is thus established, the opponent raises [the question]: Is the causation of doubt [a property] of the two [reasons] combined or of each separately?

body.text: yadi samastayoḥ saṃdehahetutvaṃ tadāsādhāraṇānna bhidyate / śrāvaṇatvaṃ cāsādhāraṇatvenoktam / atha vyastayostadapi na / vyastayoḥ samyagdhetutvāt / atrocyate / samastayoreva saṃdehahetutvam / nanūktam asādhāraṇānna bhidyate / tanna / yato bhidyata eva / parasparasāpekṣo viruddhāvyabhicārī ceti / ekakaḥ asahāyo 'sādhāraṇaḥ / sa cānenāṃśenācāryeṇa bhinna upātta iti tasmādadoṣaḥ / uktaṃ ca mūlagranthe dvāvapyetāveko 'naikāntikaḥ samuditāveva / anudbhāvite tu tadabhāva iti / atra bahu vaktavyam / tattu nocyate / saṃkṣeparucisattvānugrahārtho 'yamārambhaḥ / ityukto 'naikāntikaḥ // sāṃprataṃ viruddhamāhaḥ viruddhaścatuḥprakāra ityādi / virudhyate sa viruddhaḥ / tathā hyayaṃ dharmasvarūpādiviparītasādhanārddharmeṇa dharmiṇā vā virudhyata eveti catuḥprakāraścaturbhedaḥ / tadyathā / dharmasvarūpaviparītasādhana ityādi / tadyatheti bhedopanyāsārthaḥ / śabdārthamudāharaṇādhikāra eva vakṣyāmaḥ / tatra dharmetyādi / tatra dharmasvarūpaviparītasādhano yathā nityeti pūrvavat / dharmaḥ paryāya ityanarthāntaram / tasya svarūpamasādhāraṇāmātmalakṣaṇa dharmasvarūpaṃ tasya viparītasādhana iti samāsaḥ / evaṃ śeṣeṣvapi draṣṭavyamiti / adhunodāharaṇamāha / yathā nitya śabdaḥ kṛtakatvāt prayatnānantarīyakatvādvā ityayaṃ heturvipakṣa eva bhāvadviruddhaḥ / atra dharmasvarūpanityatvam / ayaṃ ca hetuviparītamanityatvaṃ sādhayati / tenaivāvinābhūtatvāt / tathā cāha / vipakṣa eva bhāvādviruddhaḥ / āha ayamapakṣadharmatvādasiddhānna viśiṣyate kathaṃ viruddha iti? / atrocyate / nāvaśyaṃ pakṣadharma eva viruddhatā anyathāpyācāryapravṛtteḥ / adhikṛtayogajñāpakāt / na cāyamasiddhānna viśiṣyate iti /
body.translated_text: If both [reasons] taken together cause doubt, then [this fallacy] would not differ from the exclusive (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>). And audibility has been stated as [an example of] the exclusive [reason]. But if [it is argued that] taken separately [they do not cause doubt] — that also is not [correct], because taken separately each is a valid reason. To this it is said: it is precisely when taken together that they cause doubt. [Objection:] But it was said that [this] does not differ from the exclusive. [Reply:] That is not so, because it does indeed differ: the contradictory non-deviating (<s>viruddhāvyabhicārī</s>) [reason] involves mutual dependence [of two opposing reasons], whereas the exclusive [reason] is single, without a companion. And it has been distinguished by the <s>Ācārya</s> (master) in this respect, and therefore there is no fault. And it has been said in the root text: 'These two also are one inconclusive [reason], only when combined; but when [the counterpart] has not been produced, it [i.e., the fallacy] is absent.' Here much could be said, but it is not stated — this undertaking is for the benefit of those inclined to brevity. Thus the inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) [reason] has been explained. Now he states the contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>) [reason]: 'The contradictory is of four kinds' and so on. That which contradicts is 'contradictory' (<s>viruddha</s>). For this [reason] indeed contradicts by establishing the opposite of the essential nature of the property, etc., or by the property or property-bearer — hence it is of four kinds, [meaning] four divisions. Namely: 'establishing the opposite of the essential nature of the property' and so on. 'Namely' (<s>tadyathā</s>) is for the purpose of presenting the divisions. We shall explain the word-meaning in the section on examples itself. Therein, 'the property' and so on — therein, '[the reason] establishing the opposite of the essential nature of the property, for example, [sound is] eternal' — as before. 'Property' (<s>dharma</s>) and 'synonym' (<s>paryāya</s>) are not different in meaning. Its essential nature is its own exclusive self-characteristic — this is 'the essential nature of the property'; establishing its opposite is the compound. The rest should be understood similarly. Now he states the example: 'For example, sound is eternal, because of being produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>), or because of arising immediately after effort (<s>prayatnānantarīyakatva</s>)' — this reason, being present only in the counter-thesis (<s>vipakṣa</s>), is contradictory by its [actual] existence [there]. Here, the essential nature of the property is eternality; and this reason establishes the opposite — non-eternality — because it is invariably concomitant with that alone. Accordingly he says: 'It is contradictory because of its [actual] existence only in the counter-thesis.' [Objection:] He says — since this [reason] is not a property of the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>), it does not differ from the unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>); how then is it contradictory? [Reply:] To this it is said — contradiction does not necessarily pertain only to a property of the thesis; it can be otherwise too, from the <s>Ācārya</s>'s practice, because [the classification] serves to indicate the applicable connection. And this [reason] is not indistinguishable from the unestablished.

body.text: viparyayasādhakatvenāsiddheḥ / etatpradhānatvāccopanyāsasya / anyathānaikāntikasyāpyasiddhatvaprasaṅgaḥ / nityatvādisādhanatvena prameyatvādīnāmapi asiddhatvāt / ityalaṃ prasaṅgena / gamanikāmātrametat / dharmaviśeṣaviparītasādhana ityasyodāharaṇaṃ yathā parārthāścakṣurādayaḥ saṃghātatvāt śayanāsanādyaṅgavat iti / kaḥ punarevamāha? / sāṃkhyo bauddhaṃ prati / iha cakṣurādayo dharmiṇaḥ / ādiśabdāt śeṣendiyamahadahaṃṅkārādiparigrahaḥ / pārārthyaṃ sādhyadharma / asya ca viśeṣo 'saṃhataparārthatvamiṣṭam / anyathā siddhasādhyatāpattyā prayogavaikalyaprasaṅgaḥ / saṃghātatvāditi hetuḥ / tatra dvayorbahūnāṃ vā melakaḥ saṃghātastasya bhāvaḥ saṃghātatvaṃ tasmātsaṃghātatvāt / śayanāsanādyaṅgavaditi dṛṣṭāntaḥ / śayanaṃ palyaṅkādi / āsanamāsandakādi / tadaṅgāni pratītānyeva / yathaitadaṅgāni saṃghātatvāddevadattādiparārthāni vartante evaṃ cakṣurādayo 'pīti bhāvārthaḥ / adhunā viruddhamāha /
body.translated_text: Because of the non-establishment in respect of proving the opposite — and because this [proving the opposite] is the primary purpose of the discussion. Otherwise, even the inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) [reason] would be subject to the charge of being unestablished, since things like 'being a knowable object' (<s>prameyatva</s>) would also be unestablished as proofs of eternality and the like. So enough of this digression; this is merely an indication of the analysis. The example of '[the reason] establishing the opposite of a specific [qualification of the] property' (<s>dharmaviśeṣaviparītasādhana</s>) is: 'The eyes and other [sense organs] are for the purpose of another, because of being composite (<s>saṃghātatva</s>) — like the parts of a bed and seat and so on.' And who says this? A <s>Sāṃkhya</s> [philosopher] toward a Buddhist. Here, the eyes and other [organs] are the property-bearers. By the word 'and so on' (<s>ādi</s>), the remaining sense organs, <s>mahat</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), and so on are included. Being-for-the-purpose-of-another (<s>pārārthya</s>) is the property to be proved. And its specific [qualification] is: being for the purpose of another in an uncomposed [state] is what is intended. Otherwise, there would be the fault of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhyatā</s>), resulting in a deficiency of the argument. 'Because of being composite' (<s>saṃghātatvāt</s>) is the reason. Therein, the coming together of two or many is a composite (<s>saṃghāta</s>); its nature is compositeness (<s>saṃghātatva</s>) — therefore, because of compositeness. 'Like the parts of a bed and seat and so on' is the example. A bed is a couch and the like; a seat is a chair and the like. Their parts are well-known. Just as these parts, because of being composite, serve the purpose of another such as <s>Devadatta</s>, so too the eyes and other [organs] — this is the intended meaning. Now he states the contradictory [reason]:

body.text: ayamityādi / ayaṃ hetuḥ saṃghātatvalakṣano yathā yena prakāreṇa pārārthyaṃ parārthabhāvaṃ cakṣurādīnāṃ sādhayati tathā tenaiva prakāreṇa saṃhatatvamapi sāvayavatvamapi parasyātmanaḥ sādhayati / tenāpyavinābhūtatvāt / tathā cāha / ubhayatrāvyabhicārāt / ubhayatreti parārthe saṃhatatve ca avyabhicārād gamakatvādityarthaḥ / tathā caivamapi vaktuṃ śakyata eva saṃhataparārthāścakṣurādayaḥ saṃghātatvāt śayanāsanādyaṅgavaditi / śayanāsaṇādyaṅgāni hi saṃhatasya karacaraṇorugrīvādimata evārthaṃ kurvanti nānyasya / tathopalabdheriti / āha vipakṣa eva bhāvādviruddha iti sāmānyaṃ viruddhalakṣaṇaṃ tatkathamihopapadyate? iti / ucyate / asaṃhataparavipakṣo hi saṃhata iti tatraiva vṛttidarśanāt / kiṃ nopapadyate? / ākṣepaparihārau pūrvavat // dharmisvarūpaviparītetyādi / dharmā asya vidyante iti dharmī / udāharaṇaṃ tu yathā na dravyamityādi / kaḥ punarevamāha? / vaiśeṣiko bauddhānprati / kena punaḥ saṃbandhena? iti / ucyate / tasya siddhānto dravyaguṇakarmasāmānyaviśeṣasamavāyāḥ ṣaṭpadārthāḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This [reason],' etc. — This reason, characterized by 'being a composite' (<s>saṃghātatva</s>), in the same manner by which it establishes the 'being for the sake of another' (<s>pārārthya</s>) of the eyes and so forth, in that very same manner it also establishes the 'being composite' (<s>saṃhatatva</s>), i.e. 'having parts' (<s>sāvayavatva</s>), of the other [entity, namely] the self (<s>ātman</s>) — because it [the reason] is invariably concomitant with that [property] too. And accordingly [the text] states: 'Because of non-deviation in both [cases]' (<s>ubhayatrāvyabhicārāt</s>) — 'in both' means in [both] being-for-another and being-composite — 'because of non-deviation' means because of being an indicator; that is the meaning. And thus it can also be stated as follows: 'The eyes and so forth are composite and for the sake of another, because of being aggregates — like the limbs of a bed, seat, and such.' For the limbs of a bed, seat, and so forth — belonging to the composite [body] of hands, feet, thighs, neck, and so on — do indeed serve a purpose.

body.text: tataḥ pṛthvyāpastejovāyurākāśaṃ kālo digātmā mana iti dravyāṇi / guṇāścaturviśatiḥ / rūparasagandhasparśasaṃkhyāparimāṇāni pṛthaktvaṃ saṃyogavibhāgau paratvāparatve buddhiḥ sukhaduḥkhecchādveṣāḥ prayatnaśceti sūtroktāḥ / caśabdāt dravatvaṃ gurutvaṃ saṃskāraḥ sneho dharmādharmau śabdaśceti / evaṃ caturviśati rguṇāḥ / pañca karmāṇi / tadyathā utkṣepaṇamavakṣepaṇamākuñcanaṃ prasāraṇaṃ gamanamiti karmāṇi / gamanagrahaṇābdhramaṇarecanaspandanādyavarodhaḥ / sāmānyaṃ dvividhaṃ paramaparaṃ ceti / tatra paraṃ sattā bhāvo mahāsāmānyamiti cocyate / aparaṃ dravyatvādi / tatra sattā dravyaguṇakarmabhyo 'rthāntaram / kathāpunaryuktyā? ityatrāha / na dravyaṃ bhāvaḥ ekadravyavattvāditi hetuḥ / sāmānyaviśeṣavaditi dṛṣṭāntaḥ / adhunā bhāvārtha ucyate / na dravyaṃ bhāvaḥ / dravyādanya ityarthaḥ / ekadravyavattvādityatra ekaṃ ca taddravyaṃ ca ekadravyamasyāstīti āśrayabhūtamiti ekadravyavān /
body.translated_text: Then [the Vaiśeṣika categories are enumerated]: the substances (<s>dravya</s>) are earth, water, fire, air, space (<s>ākāśa</s>), time, direction, self (<s>ātman</s>), and mind (<s>manas</s>). And the qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) are twenty-four. The [first seventeen] stated in the <s>sūtra</s>s are: form (<s>rūpa</s>), taste (<s>rasa</s>), smell (<s>gandha</s>), touch (<s>sparśa</s>), number (<s>saṃkhyā</s>), dimension (<s>parimāṇa</s>), separateness (<s>pṛthaktva</s>), conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) and disjunction (<s>vibhāga</s>), priority (<s>paratva</s>) and posteriority (<s>aparatva</s>), cognition (<s>buddhi</s>), pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and pain (<s>duḥkha</s>), desire (<s>icchā</s>) and aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and effort (<s>prayatna</s>). By the word 'and' [are indicated additionally]: fluidity (<s>dravatva</s>), heaviness (<s>gurutva</s>), dispositional tendency (<s>saṃskāra</s>), viscidity (<s>sneha</s>), merit (<s>dharma</s>) and demerit (<s>adharma</s>), and sound (<s>śabda</s>). Thus the qualities are twenty-four. The actions (<s>karman</s>) are five: namely, throwing upward (<s>utkṣepaṇa</s>), throwing downward (<s>avakṣepaṇa</s>), contraction (<s>ākuñcana</s>), expansion (<s>prasāraṇa</s>), and locomotion (<s>gamana</s>). By 'locomotion' are included also revolution, ejection, vibration, and so forth. The universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) is twofold: supreme (<s>para</s>) and non-supreme (<s>apara</s>). Therein...

body.text: samānādhikaraṇābdahuvrīhiḥ kadācitkarmadhārayaḥ sarvadhanādyartha iti vacanāt / tadbhāvastattvaṃ tasmādekadravyavattvāt / ekasmindravye vartamānatvādityarthaḥ / vaiśeṣikasya hi adravyaṃ dravyaṃ anekadravyaṃ ca dravyam / tatrādravyaṃ dravyamākāśakāladigātmanaḥ paramāṇavaḥ / anekadravyaṃ tu dvayaṇukādiskandhāḥ / ekadravyaṃ tu dravyameva nāsti / ekadravyavāṃśca bhāvaḥ / ityato dravyalakṣaṇavilakṣaṇatvāt na dravyaṃ bhāva iti / dṛṣṭāntaḥ sāmānyaviśeṣaḥ / sa ca dravyatvaguṇatvakarmatvalakṣaṇaḥ / dravyatvaṃ hi navasu dravyeṣu vartamānatvātsāmānyaṃ guṇakarmabhyo vyāvartamānatvādviśeṣaḥ / evaṃ guṇatvakarmatvayorapi bhāvanā kāryeti / tataśca sāmānyaṃ ca tadviśeṣaśca sa iti sāmānyaviśeṣastena tulyaṃ vartata iti sāmānyaviśeṣavat / dravyatvavadityarthaḥ / tataścaitadukte bhavati / yathā navasu dravyeṣu pratyekaṃ vartamānaṃ dravyaṃ na bhavati kiṃtu sāmānyaviśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ dravyatvameva evaṃ bhāvo 'pītyabhiprāyaḥ / āha yadi nāma dravyaṃ na bhavati tathāpi guṇobhaviṣyati karma ca ityetadapi nirācikīrṣurāha / guṇakarmasu ca bhāvāt / tataśca na guṇo bhāvaḥ guṇeṣu bhāvād guṇatvavat / yadi ca bhāvo guṇaḥ syānna tarhi guṇeṣu varteta nirguṇatvād guṇānām / vartate ca guṇeṣu bhāvaḥ / san guṇa iti pratīteḥ / tathā na karma bhāvaḥ karmasu bhāvātkarmatvavat / yadi ca bhāvaḥ karma syāt na tarhi karmasu varteta niṣkarmakatvātkarmaṇām / vartate ca karmasu bhāvaḥ / satkarmeti pratīteḥ / vyatyayopanyāsastu pratijñāhetvorvicitranyāyapradarśanārtham / ityevaṃ vaiśeṣikeṇokte bauddha āha / ayaṃ ca hetustriprakāro 'pi yathā dravyādipratiṣedhaṃ sādhayati tathā bhāvasya dharmiṇo 'bhāvatvamapi sādhayati /
body.translated_text: [This is] a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound with co-referential terms, sometimes a <s>karmadhāraya</s>, according to the statement 'meaning all wealth etc.' Its state (<s>bhāva</s>) is its nature (<s>tattva</s>); therefore, 'because of inhering in a single substance' (<s>ekadravyavattvāt</s>) — the meaning is: because of occurring in a single substance. For according to the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>, [there are:] non-substance-substance, substance, and many-substance substance. Therein, non-substance substance [refers to] space, time, direction, self, and atoms. Many-substance [refers to] dyads and other aggregates. But single-substance substance simply does not exist [as a substance]. And <s>bhāva</s> (existence) inheres in a single substance. Therefore, because of having a characteristic different from the defining mark of substance, <s>bhāva</s> is not a substance. The example is <s>sāmānyaviśeṣa</s> (universal-particular). And this has the defining marks of substance-ness, quality-ness, and action-ness. For substance-ness, by occurring in the nine substances, is a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), and by being excluded from qualities and actions, is a particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>). The same should be understood for quality-ness and action-ness. Therefore, that which is both universal and particular is <s>sāmānyaviśeṣa</s>; 'like <s>sāmānyaviśeṣa</s>' means: it exists equally [with it] — meaning: like substance-ness. Accordingly, when this is stated, the purport is: just as that which occurs individually in each of the nine substances is not a [further] substance, but is merely substance-ness of the nature of universal-particular — so too is <s>bhāva</s> (existence). He says: Even if it is not a substance, it might be a quality or an action — wishing to refute this too, he says: 'And because of being present in qualities and actions.' Therefore, <s>bhāva</s> is not a quality, because of being present in qualities — like quality-ness. For if <s>bhāva</s> were a quality, it would not then occur in qualities, because qualities are without [further] qualities. But <s>bhāva</s> does occur in qualities — from the cognition 'the quality exists.' Likewise, <s>bhāva</s> is not an action, because of being present in actions — like action-ness. For if <s>bhāva</s> were an action, it would not then occur in actions, because actions are without [further] actions. But <s>bhāva</s> does occur in actions — from the cognition 'the action exists.' The reversed presentation [of thesis and reason] is for the purpose of displaying varied modes of reasoning in thesis and reason. When the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> speaks thus, the Buddhist says: This reason, though threefold, just as it proves the negation of substance and the like, also proves the non-existence of <s>bhāva</s> as the <s>dharmin</s> (subject).

body.text: tenāpyavinābhūtatvāt / tathā cāha / ubhayatrāvyabhicārāt / ubhayatra dravyādipratiṣedhe bhāvābhāve ca gamakatvāt / tathā ca / yatathaidbaktuṃ śakyate na dravyaṃ bhāvaḥ ekadravyatvāt dravyatvavat evamidamapi śakyate bhāvo bhāva eva na bhavati ekadravyatvāt dravyatvavat / na ca dravyatvaṃ bhāvaḥ sāmānyaviśeṣatvāt / evaṃ na guṇaḥ guṇeṣu bhāvāt guṇatvavat / atrāpi bhāvo bhāva eva na bhavati guṇeṣu bhāvāt guṇatvavat / na ca guṇatvaṃ bhāvaḥ sāmānyaviśeṣatvādeva / evaṃ na karma bhāvaḥ karmasu bhāvāt karmatvavat atrāpi bhāvo bhāva eva na bhavati karmasu bhāvāt karmatvavat / na ca karmatvaṃ bhāvaḥ sāmānyaviśeṣatvāt / sāmānyaviruddhalakṣaṇayojanā tu bhāvavipakṣatvātsāmānyaviśeṣasya sukaraiva / āha ayamasiddhānna viśiṣyate iti kathaṃ viruddhaḥ? / tathāhi / na bhāvo nāma dravyādivyatiriktaḥ kaścidasti saugatānām / tadabhāvāccaśrayāsiddha eva heturiti / atrocyate satyametat / kiṃtu paraprasiddho 'pi vipakṣamātravyāpī viruddha iti nidarśanārthatvāt / ekasminnapi cānekadoṣajātyupanipātanāt tadbhedadarśanārthatvānna doṣa iti / āha evamaviruddhabhāvaḥ sarvatra viśeṣaviruddhabhāvāditi / na / virodhino 'dhikṛtahetvanvitadṛṣṭāntabalenaiva nivṛteḥ / tathāpyanityaḥ śabdaḥ pākyatvādghatavat pākyaḥ śabda iti viruddhapreraṇāyāṃ kṛtakatvānvitāpākyapaṭādidṛṣṭāntāntarasāmarthyāttannivṛttyā na viruddhatā / anivṛttau cābhyupagamyata eva /
body.translated_text: Because of its inseparable connection with that [consequence] as well. And thus he says: 'Because of non-deviation in both cases.' Because of being indicative of both the negation of substance and the like and of the non-existence of <s>bhāva</s>. And thus, just as one can say '<s>bhāva</s> is not a substance, because of inhering in a single substance — like substance-ness,' so too one can say: '<s>bhāva</s>, being nothing but <s>bhāva</s>, does not exist [as a substance], because of inhering in a single substance — like substance-ness.' And substance-ness is not <s>bhāva</s>, because it is a universal-particular. Likewise, <s>bhāva</s> is not a quality, because of being present in qualities — like quality-ness; here too, <s>bhāva</s>, being nothing but <s>bhāva</s>, does not exist [as a quality], because of being present in qualities — like quality-ness. And quality-ness is not <s>bhāva</s>, because it is a universal-particular. Likewise, <s>bhāva</s> is not an action, because of being present in actions — like action-ness; here too, <s>bhāva</s>, being nothing but <s>bhāva</s>, does not exist [as an action], because of being present in actions — like action-ness. And action-ness is not <s>bhāva</s>, because it is a universal-particular. The construction with the contradictory universal [is possible because] it is easy, since <s>sāmānyaviśeṣa</s> is in the counter-class of <s>bhāva</s>. He asks: This is no different from the unestablished [reason] — how is it contradictory? For indeed, according to the Buddhists (<s>Saugatās</s>), there is no <s>bhāva</s> distinct from substance and the like; and because of its absence, the reason is simply 'unestablished as to the substrate' (<s>āśrayāsiddha</s>). To this it is replied: This is true; however, [a reason] which is well-known to the opponent yet pervades only the counter-class (<s>vipakṣa</s>) is [classified as] 'contradictory' — since this is for the purpose of illustration. And because in a single [case], multiple fallacy-types can be superimposed, and it is for the purpose of showing those distinctions — there is no fault. He says: Thus the non-contradictory state [of the reason] is [present] everywhere, because of the presence of the specifically-contradictory state. No — because the contradictory [interpretation] is defeated by the force of an example connected with the relevant non-contradictory reason. Even so, [consider:] 'Sound is impermanent, because of being fire-able, like a pot; sound is fire-able' — when the contradictory [reading] is urged, by the force of another example such as cloth and the like, which are non-fire-able yet connected with the [reason of] 'being produced,' that [contradictory reading] is defeated, and there is no contradiction. If it is not defeated, then it is simply conceded.

body.text: aśakyā ceha tannivṛttirekadravyavatvasya tadvyatirekeṇānyatrāvṛtteriti / atra bahu vaktavyam / alaṃ prasaṅgena // dharmiviśeṣaviparītasādhano yathā / dharmī bhāva eva tadviśeṣaḥ satpratyayakartṛtvam / yata uktaṃ saditi yato dravyaguṇakarmasu sā sattā / tadviparītasādhano yathā / ayameva heturekadravyavattvākhyaḥ asminneva pūrvapakṣe na dravyaṃ bhāva ityādilakṣaṇe asyaiva dharmiṇo bhāvākhyasya yo viśeṣo dharmaḥ satpratyayakartṛtvaṃ nāma tadviparitamasatpratyayakartṛtvamapi sādhayati / tenāpi vyāpyatvāt / tathā hyetadapi vaktuṃ śakyata eva bhāvaḥ satpratyayakartā na bhavati ekadravyavattvādravyatvat / na ca dravyatvaṃ satpratyayakartṛ dravyapratyayakartṛtvāt / evaṃ guṇakarmabhāvahetvorapi vācyam / ata evamuktam- ubhayatrāvyabhicārāditi / bhāvitārthameva / ākṣepaparihārau pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: And here the exclusion of that [property 'being in one substance'] is impossible, because 'being in one substance' does not occur anywhere else apart from that [particular case]. Much more could be said on this; enough of this digression. [The contradictory reason that] establishes the opposite of a specific property of the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer): The <s>dharmin</s> is <s>bhāva</s> (existence/being) itself; its specific property is 'being the cause of the cognition "existent" (<s>satpratyayakartṛtva</s>)' — since it is said '<s>sat</s> (existent),' and therefore that <s>sattā</s> (existence) [inheres] in substance, quality, and action. [The reason] establishes the opposite of that [specific property], thus: this very reason called 'being in one substance,' in this very prima facie position — in the characterization 'existence is not a substance' — also establishes the opposite of the specific property (<s>dharma</s>) of this very <s>dharmin</s> called <s>bhāva</s>, namely 'not being the cause of the cognition "existent" (<s>asatpratyayakartṛtva</s>),' because it is also pervaded by that [opposite property]. For this too can be stated: '<s>Bhāva</s> (existence) is not the cause of the cognition "existent," because of being in one substance, like substancehood (<s>dravyatva</s>).' And <s>dravyatva</s> is not the cause of the cognition 'existent' because it is the cause of the cognition 'substance.' The same should be said for [the reasons pertaining to] quality, action, and existence. Therefore it has been said: 'because of non-deviation in both cases.' The meaning has already been brought out. The objection and its resolution [are to be understood] as before.

body.text: uktā hetvābhāsāḥ / sāṃprataṃ dṛṣṭāntābhāsānāmavasaraḥ / te ucyante / tatra yathā dṛṣṭānto dvividhaḥ evaṃ mūlabhedavyapekṣayā tadābhāso 'pi tathā / āha / dṛṣṭāntābhaso dvividhaḥ / sādharmyeṇa vaidharmyeṇa ca / dṛṣṭānta uktalakṣaṇaḥ / dṛṣṭāntavadābhāsa iti dṛṣṭāntābhāsaḥ / dṛṣṭāntapratirūpaka ityarthaḥ / tatra sādharmyeṇa tāvaddṛṣṭāntābhāsaḥ pañcaprakāraḥ pañcabhedaḥ tadyathā / sādhanadharmāsiddha ityādi / tadyatheti bhedopadarśanārthaḥ / sādhanadharmo heturasiddho nāstītyucyate / tataśca sādhanadharmo 'siddho 'smin so 'yaṃ sādhanadharmāsiddhaḥ / na tu bahubrīhau niṣṭhāntaṃ pūrvaṃ nipatatīti kṛtvāsiddhasādhanadharmā iti / na vāhitāgnyādiṣu vacanāt / āhitāgnyādeścākṛtigaṇatvādvikalpavṛtteriti / anye tu sādhanadharmeṇa rahitatvādasiddhaḥ sādhanadharmāsiddhaḥ iti vyācakṣate / na caitadatiśobhanam / evaṃ sādhyobhayadharmāsiddhayorapi bhāvanīyam / anvayādiśabdārthaṃ tūdāharaṇādhikāre vakṣyāmaḥ / sa cāvasaraḥ prāpta eveti yathākramaṃ nirdiśyate / tatra sādhanadharmāsiddho yathā / nityaḥ śabdo 'mūrtatvāt / yathetyudāharaṇopanyasārthaḥ / nityaḥ śabda iti pratijñā pakṣaḥ / amūrtatvāditi hetuḥ / anvayamāha /
body.translated_text: The <s>hetvābhāsa</s>s (pseudo-reasons) have been stated. Now it is the occasion for the <s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s>s (pseudo-examples). These are stated. Therein, just as the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) is of two kinds, so too, with respect to the fundamental division, its semblance is also [of two kinds]. He says: 'The <s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s> (pseudo-example) is of two kinds: by similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) and by dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>).' The <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> has the stated definition. '<s>Dṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s>' means 'a semblance that resembles a <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>' — the meaning is: a counterfeit of an example. Therein, first, the <s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s> by similarity is of five varieties, five divisions, namely: 'that in which the proving property (<s>sādhanadharmā</s>) is unestablished,' and so forth. The [expression] 'namely' (<s>tadyathā</s>) is for the purpose of displaying the divisions. 'The proving property' means the reason (<s>hetu</s>); 'unestablished' means 'absent,' it is said. And therefore, 'that in which the proving property is unestablished' — that is the <s>sādhanadharmāsiddha</s>. But one should not [analyze it] as '<s>asiddhasādhanadharmā</s>' on the grounds that in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound the past participle comes first — for this is stated in [the class of] <s>āhitāgni</s> and similar [compounds]. And [the class of] <s>āhitāgni</s> and the like, being an open-ended class (<s>akṛtigaṇa</s>), has variable application. Others explain it as: '<s>sādhanadharmāsiddha</s>' means 'unestablished because of being devoid of the proving property.' But this is not very elegant. The same should be understood for [the cases where] the <s>sādhya</s>-property and both properties are unestablished. The meaning of the words '<s>anvaya</s>' and so on we shall state in the section on examples. And since that occasion has indeed arrived, [the pseudo-examples] are indicated in order. Therein, [the first:] 'That in which the proving property is unestablished' — for example: 'Sound is permanent, because of incorporeality (<s>amūrtatva</s>).' The word '<s>yathā</s>' (for example) is for the purpose of introducing the illustration. 'Permanent' —

body.text: yadamūrtaṃ vastu tannityaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathā paramāṇuriti sādharmyadṛṣṭāntatvam / etadābhāsānāmeva prakrāntatvāt / nārtho vaidharmyeṇeti na pradarśitaḥ / ayaṃ ca sādhyasādhanadharmānugata iṣyate / iha tu sādhyadharmo 'sti na sādhanadharmaḥ / tathā cāha / paramāṇau hi sādhyaṃ nityatvamasti / antyakāraṇatvena nityatvāt / sādhanadharmo 'mūrtatvaṃ nāsti / kutaḥ / mūrtatvāt paramāṇunām / mūrtatvaṃ ca mūrtimatkāryaghaṭādyupalabdheḥ siddhamiti // sādhyadharmāsiddho yathā / nityaḥ śabdo 'mūrtatvād buddhivaditi / yadamūrtaṃ vastu tannityaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathā buddhiḥ / buddhau hi sādhanadharmo 'mūrtatvasti sādhyadharmo nityatvaṃ nāsti anityatvādbuddhoriti sūtraprayogaḥ sugama eva / vyāptiṃ darśayati / yadamūrtaṃ vastu tannityaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathā buddhiḥ / āha kathamayaṃ sādhyadharmāsiddha? iti / atrāha / buddhau hi sādhanadharmo 'mūrtatvamasti / tadamūrtatvapratīteḥ / sādhyadharmo nityatvaṃ nāsti / kutaḥ? / anityatvādbuddheriti // ubhayāsiddho dvividhaḥ / katham? ityatrāha / sannasaṃśceti / sanniti vidyamānobhayāsiddhaḥ / tataśca asanniti avidyamānobhayāsiddhaḥ / prayogo maula eva draṣṭavyaḥ / yata āha / tatra ghaṭavadīti vidyamānobhayāsiddhaḥ / tataśca nityaḥ śabdo 'mūrtatvādghaṭavadityatra na sādhyadharmo nityatvalakṣaṇaḥ nāpi sādhanadharmo 'mūrtatvalakṣaṇo 'sti anityatvānmūrtatvādghaṭasyeti / tathāākāśavadityavidyamānobhayāsiddhaḥ / tataśca nityaḥ śabdo 'mūrtatvādākāśavaditi /
body.translated_text: 'Whatever entity is formless (<s>amūrta</s>) is eternal — as observed in the case of the atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>)' — this is [intended] as a concordant example (<s>sādharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>). Since only the semblances of examples are being discussed here, there is no need for a discordant [example]; hence it is not shown. And this [example] is expected to possess both the property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharma</s>) and the proving property (<s>sādhanadharma</s>). But here [in this case], the property to be proved exists [in the example] but not the proving property. Accordingly [the text] states: In the atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>), the property to be proved — eternality — does exist, because it is eternal by virtue of being an ultimate cause. But the proving property — formlessness (<s>amūrtatva</s>) — does not exist [in the atom]. Why? Because atoms are corporeal (<s>mūrta</s>). And corporeality is established because corporeal effects such as pots and the like are observed [to be produced from atoms]. [Next:] 'The one in which the property to be proved is unestablished' — for example: 'Sound is eternal, because of being formless — like cognition (<s>buddhi</s>)...'

body.text: nanvayamubhayasabdhāvātkathamubhayāsiddha ityāśaṅkayāha / tadasattvavādinaṃ prati / ākāśāsattvavādinaṃ bauddhaṃ prati / sāṃkhyasyetyarthaḥ / sati hi tasminnityatvādidharmacintā nānyatheti // ananvaya ityādi / avidyamāno 'nvayo 'nanvayaḥ / apradarśitānvaya ityarthaḥ / anvayo 'nugamo vyāptiriti anarthāntaram / lakṣaṇamāha / yatretyādi / yatretyabhidheyamāha / vinānvayena vinā vyāptidarśanena sādhyasādhanayoḥ sādhyahetvorityarthaḥ / sahabhāva ekavṛttimātram / pradarśyate kathyate ākhyāyate / na vīpsayā sādhyānugateṣu heturiti / udāharaṇamāha / yathā ghaṭe kṛtakatvamanityaṃ ca dṛṣṭamiti / ghaṭaḥ kṛtakatvānityatvayorāśraya iti / evaṃ sati āśrayāśrayibhāvamātrābhidhānādanyatra vyabhicārasaṃbhavādiṣṭārthasādhakatvānupapattiḥ / viparītānvaya ityādi / viparīto viparyayavṛttiranvayo 'nugamo yasmin tathāvidhaḥ / udāharaṇamāha / yatkṛtakaṃ tadanityaṃ dṛṣṭamiti vaktavye yadanityaṃ tatkṛtakaṃ dṛṣṭamiti bravīti / evaṃ prāksādhanadharmamanuccārya sādhyadharmamuccārayati / āha / evamapi ko doṣaḥ? iti / ucyate / nyāyamudrāvyatikramaḥ / anyatra vyāptivyabhicārāt / yathā hyanityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatnāntarīyakatvādiyatra yadyadanityaṃ tattatprayatnāntarīyakam / anityānāmapi vidyudādīnāmaprayatnānantarīyakatvāt / ityalaṃ prasaṅgena / ayaṃ sādharmyadṛṣṭāntābhāsaḥ samāptaḥ // vaidharmyeṇāpi / na kevalaṃ sādharmyeṇaiva / kim? / dṛṣṭāntābhāsaḥ / prāṅnirūpitaśabdārthaḥ / pañcaprakāraḥ / tadyathā sādhyāvyāvṛtta ityādi / tatra sādhyaṃ pratītaṃ tadavyāvṛttasmāditi sādhyāvyāvṛttaḥ / ākṣepaparihārau pūrvavat / evaṃ sādhanobhayāvyāvṛttayorapi vaktavyam / avyatirekādiśabdārthaṃ tūdāharaṇādhikāra eva vakṣyāmaḥ / sa cāvasaraḥ prāpta eva // tatra sādhyāvyāvṛttaḥ yathā nityaḥ śabdo 'mūrtatvātparamāṇuvat / yathetyudāharaṇopanyāsārthaḥ / nityaḥ śabda iti pratijñā / amūrtatvāditi hetuḥ / vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntābhāsasya prakrāntatvātsādharmyadṛṣṭānto noktaḥ / abhyūhyaścākāśādiḥ /
body.translated_text: But if this [instance, i.e., space,] is non-existent for both [parties], how is it 'unestablished for both' (<s>ubhayāsiddha</s>)? Anticipating this doubt, he says: 'With respect to one who asserts the non-existence of that' — i.e., with respect to the Buddhist who asserts the non-existence of space — the meaning is: from the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>'s [perspective]. For only when that [space] exists can there be deliberation on properties such as permanence and so forth — not otherwise. [Next:] 'Without positive concomitance' (<s>ananvaya</s>) and so on. 'Non-existent <s>anvaya</s>' (<s>ananvaya</s>) means the [positive] concomitance is absent — i.e., 'whose positive concomitance has not been demonstrated.' <s>Anvaya</s>, <s>anugama</s>, and <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) are synonymous. He states the definition: 'Where' and so on. [He explains] what is to be expressed by 'where': 'Without <s>anvaya</s>' means without demonstrating the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) and the <s>sādhana</s> (probans), i.e., of the probandum and the reason. 'Co-presence' (<s>sahabhāva</s>) is mere co-occurrence. '[It] is demonstrated, stated, declared — not in the manner of repeated showing that the reason follows the probandum [across instances].' He gives an example: 'For instance, in a pot, the-being-produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) and impermanence have been observed.' The pot is the locus of both being-produced and impermanence. But when this is so, since only the relation of substratum and superstratum is stated, the possibility of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) elsewhere [arises], and thus the failure to establish the intended meaning [results]. [Next:] 'Reversed concomitance' (<s>viparītānvaya</s>) and so on. That in which the <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) has a reversed operation — [an example] is such. He gives an example: Instead of saying 'Whatever is produced, that is impermanent — as observed,' one says 'Whatever is impermanent, that is produced — as observed.' Thus, without first stating the property of the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>), one states the property of the probandum (<s>sādhya</s>). One objects: Even so, what is the fault? It is said: It is a transgression of the logical convention (<s>nyāyamudrā</s>), because of the deviation of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) elsewhere. For example, 'Sound is impermanent because of being the consequence of effort' — wherever there is impermanence, there is being the consequence of effort [does not hold], because even impermanent things like lightning and the like are not the consequence of effort. But enough of this digression. This [section on] the semblances of the homologous example (<s>sādharmyadṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s>) is complete. 'By dissimilarity also' — not only by similarity. What? — a semblance of example. Its word-meaning has been analyzed previously. It is of five kinds. Namely: 'That in which the probandum is not excluded' (<s>sādhyāvyāvṛtta</s>) and so on. Therein, the probandum is known; 'not excluded from that' means <s>sādhyāvyāvṛtta</s>. The objection and its resolution are as before. The same is to be said regarding 'that in which the means of proof is not excluded' and 'that in which both are not excluded.' But the meaning of words like <s>avyatireka</s> and the like we shall explain in the section on examples itself — and that occasion has indeed arrived. Among those, the <s>sādhyāvyāvṛtta</s> [semblance]: For example, 'Sound is permanent because of incorporeality — like an atom.' 'For example' is for the purpose of introducing the illustration. 'Sound is permanent' is the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>). 'Because of incorporeality' is the reason (<s>hetu</s>). Since the semblance of the dissimilar example is under discussion, the similar example is not stated, but it can be supplied — such as space and the like.

body.text: vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntastu paramāṇuḥ / ayaṃ ca sādhyasādhanobhayadharmavikalaḥ samyagiṣyate / yata uktam / sādhyābhāve hetorabhāva eva kathyate ityādi / na cāyaṃ tathetyāha ca / paramāṇorhi sakāśāt / sādhanadharmo hetuḥ / tameva darśayati amūrtatvamiti / vyāvṛttaṃ nivṛttam / kutaḥ? / mūrtatvātparamāṇunām / sādhyadharmo nityatvaṃ tanna vyāvṛttam / kutaḥ? / nityatvātparamāṇūnām / āha / sādharmyadṛṣṭāntābhāseṣvādau sādhanadharmāsiddha uktaḥ iha sādhyāvyāvṛtta iti kimarthamucyate? / tasyānvayapradhānatvāt / anvayasya ca sādhanadharmapuraḥsarasādhyadharmoccāraṇarūpatvāt / vyatirekastu ubhayavyāvṛttirūpaḥ sādhyābhāve ca hetorabhāva iti / ataḥ sādhyāvyāvṛttaḥ // tathā sādhanāvyāvṛttaḥ karmavat / prayogaḥ pūrvavadeva /
body.translated_text: The dissimilar example, however, is the atom. And this [example] is correctly said to be devoid of the properties of both the probandum and the means of proof [being excluded from it]. As has been stated: 'In the absence of the probandum, the absence of the reason alone is stated,' and so on. But this [example] is not such — and he says: From the atom, indeed — the property of the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>), i.e., the reason — he demonstrates that very [property]: incorporeality — is excluded [from the atom]. From where? Because of the corporeality of atoms. But the property of the probandum — permanence — is not excluded. From where? Because of the permanence of atoms. One asks: In the semblances of the homologous example, the 'unestablished property of the means of proof' was stated first; here 'that in which the probandum is not excluded' — why is this stated [first]? Because of the primacy of <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) [in that context], and because <s>anvaya</s> has the form of stating the property of the probandum after the property of the means of proof. But <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) has the form of the exclusion of both, [stated as] 'in the absence of the probandum, there is the absence of the reason.' Therefore, [here it is] <s>sādhyāvyāvṛtta</s> [first]. Likewise, '<s>sādhanāvyāvṛtta</s> — like <s>karma</s> (action).' The formulation is as before.

body.text: vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntastu karma / tacca utkṣepaṇādi gṛhyate / tatra karmaṇaḥ sādhyaṃ nityatvaṃ vyāvṛttam / anityatvātkarmaṇaḥ / sādhanadharmo hetuḥ / tameva darśayati amūrtatvamiti / tanna vyāvṛttam / amūrtatvātkarmaṇa iti // ubhayāvyāvṛttaḥākāśavaditi / nityatvasādhakaḥ prayogaḥ paramāṇvādisādharmyadṛṣṭāntayuktaḥ pūrvavat / vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntastvākāśamiti / tato hi ākāśāt / na nityatvaṃ vyāvṛttaṃ nāpyamūrtatvam / kutaḥ? / nityatvādamūrtatvādākāśasyeti // avyatireka ityādi / avidyamānavyātirekaḥ avyatirekaḥ anidarśitavyatireka ityarthaḥ / lakṣaṇamāha / yatra vinā sādhyasādhananivṛttyā tadvipakṣabhāvo nidarśyate / yatretyabhidheyamāha / vinā sādhyasādhananivṛttyā prastutaprayoge yadanityaṃ tanmūrtaṃ dṛṣṭamityādilakṣaṇayā / tadvipakṣabhāvaḥ sādhyasādhanavipakṣabhāvamātram / nidarśyate pratipādyate iti yāvat / dṛṣṭāntamāha / yathā ghaṭe 'nityatvaṃ ca murtatvaṃ ca dṛṣṭamiti / itthaṃ hyekatrābhidheyamātrābhidhānādvaidharmyāpratipādanādarthāpattyāpi gamyate
body.translated_text: But the discordant example (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>) is action (<s>karman</s>). And that is understood as throwing upward (<s>utkṣepaṇa</s>) and so forth. In that case, the property to be proved — eternality — is excluded from action, because action is non-eternal. The proving property, i.e. the reason, [the text] shows to be 'formlessness' (<s>amūrtatva</s>); that is not excluded, because action is formless. [Next:] 'The one in which both are non-excluded — like space (<s>ākāśa</s>).' The inference establishing eternality, with the concordant example of the atom etc., is as before. But the discordant example is space (<s>ākāśa</s>). From that, i.e. from space, neither eternality is excluded nor formlessness. Why? Because space is eternal and formless.

body.text: pratipattigauravādiṣṭārthasādhakatvamiti // viparitavyatireka ityādi / viparīto viparyasto vyatireka uktalakṣaṇo yasmin sa tathāvidhaḥ / tameva darśayati / yadanityamityādi / prastutaprayoga eva tathāvidhasādharmyadṛṣṭāntayukte vyatirekamupadeśayan yadanityaṃ tanmūrtaṃ dṛṣṭa miti vaktavye yanmūrta tadanityaṃ dṛṣṭamiti bravīti / āha / evamapi ko doṣaḥ? iti / ucyate / anyatra vyabhicāraḥ / tathā hyanityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvādityatra yadaprayatnānantarīyakaṃ tannityamiti / vyatireko vidyutā vyabhicāraḥ // nigamayannāha / eṣāmityādi / yathoktarūpāṇāṃ pakṣahetudṛṣṭāntābhāsānāṃ vacanāni / kiṃ na sādhanam? / ābhāsatvādeva / kiṃ tarhi? / sādhanābhāsamiti // uktaṃ sādhanābhāsam //
body.translated_text: ...because of the cumbersomeness of cognition [in the reversed form], [it fails to be] a prover of the intended meaning. 'Reversed exclusion' (<s>viparitavyatireka</s>) and so forth. That in which the exclusion — as defined — is reversed, i.e. inverted, is of such a nature. [The text] shows this: 'Whatever is non-eternal' etc. In the very inference under discussion, when showing the exclusion together with the concordant example of such a type, instead of saying 'whatever is non-eternal, that is observed to be corporeal,' one says 'whatever is corporeal, that is observed to be non-eternal.' [An objection:] 'Even so, what is the fault?' It is replied: there is deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) elsewhere. For in the [inference] 'sound is non-eternal, because of arising immediately after effort' — the exclusion [should be] 'whatever does not arise immediately after effort is eternal'; [but in the reversed form] lightning...

body.text: adhunā dūṣaṇasyāvasaraḥ / taccātikramya bahutaravaktavyatvātpratyakṣānumāne tāvadāha / ātmapratyāyanārthaṃ punaḥ pratyakṣamanumānaṃ ca dve eva pramāṇe / pratyakṣaṃ vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇaṃ anumānaṃ ca / asamāsakaraṇaṃ vibhinnaviṣayajñāpanārtham / svalakṣaṇaviṣayameva pratyakṣam / sāmānyalakṣaṇaviṣayamevānumānam / ca samuccaye / dve eva pramāṇe ityanena saṃkhyāniyamamāha / tathāhi bauddhānāṃ dve eva pramāṇe pratyakṣānumāne / śeṣapramāṇānāmatraivāntarbhāvāt / antarbhāvaśca pramāṇasamuccayādiṣu carcitatvānneha pratanyate / adhunā pratyakṣaṇirūpaṇāyāha / tatra pratyakṣamityādi / tatreti nirdhāraṇārthaḥ / pratyakṣamiti lakṣyanirdeśaḥ / kalpanāpoḍhamiti lakṣaṇam / ayaṃ lakṣyalakṣaṇapravibhāgaḥ / tatra pratigatamakṣaṃ pratyakṣam / kalpanāpoḍhamiti / kalpanā vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇā sā apoḍhā apetā yasmāt tat kalpanāpoḍham / samāsākṣepaparihārau pūrvavat / kalpanayāpoḍhaṃ kalpanāyā vāpoḍhaṃ kalpanāpoḍham / yat iti tatsvarūpanirdeśaḥ / evaṃbhūtaṃ cārthe svalakṣaṇamapi bhavati / āha / jñānaṃ saṃvedanam / tacca nirviṣayamapi bhavati ata āha arthe viṣaye / sa ca dvidhā svalakṣaṇasāmānyalakṣaṇabhedāt / ata āha / rūpādau svalakṣaṇe ityarthaḥ / iha yaduktaṃ kalpanāpoḍhamiti tatsvarūpābhidhānata eva vyācaṣṭe nāmajātyādikalpanārahitam / tadakṣamakṣaṃ prati vartate iti pratyakṣam / tatra nāmakalpanā yathā ḍitthā iti / jātikalpanā yathā gauriti / ādiśabdena guṇakriyādravyaparigrahaḥ / tatra guṇakalpanā śukla iti / kriyākalpanā pācaka iti / dravyakalpanā daṇḍīti / ābhiḥ kalpanābhī rahitaṃ śabdarahitam / svalakṣaṇahetutvāt / uktaṃ ca / na hyarthe śabdāḥ anti tadātmāno vā yena tasminpratibhāsamāne te 'pi pratibhāserannityādi / tadakṣamityādi / tadityanena yannirdiṣṭasya parāmarśaḥ / akṣāṇīndriyāṇi /
body.translated_text: Now is the occasion for refutation (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>). But skipping that for now, since there is more to say, he first states [about] perception and inference: 'For the purpose of self-cognition, perception and inference are just two <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition).' Perception has the definition to be stated, and inference [likewise]. The separate mention is for the purpose of indicating distinct objects: perception has only the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) as its object; inference has only the universal (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>) as its object. <s>Ca</s> is for conjunction. By 'just two <s>pramāṇas</s>,' he states a numerical restriction. For indeed, according to the Buddhists, there are just two <s>pramāṇas</s> — perception and inference — because the remaining <s>pramāṇas</s> are subsumed under these very [two]. And since this subsumption has been discussed in the <s>Pramāṇasamuccaya</s> and the like, it is not elaborated here. Now, for the purpose of defining perception, he says: 'Therein, perception...' and so on. 'Therein' (<s>tatra</s>) is for specification. '<s>Pratyakṣa</s>' (perception) is the indication of the <s>lakṣya</s> (definiendum). '<s>Kalpanāpoḍha</s>' (free from conceptual construction) is the <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (definition). This is the distinction between definiendum and definition. Therein, that which is 'directed toward' (<s>prati</s>) the 'sense-organ' (<s>akṣa</s>) is '<s>pratyakṣa</s>.' '<s>Kalpanāpoḍha</s>': <s>kalpanā</s> (conceptual construction) has the definition to be stated; that from which it has been removed (<s>apoḍhā</s>) — that is <s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>. The resolution of objections concerning the compound is as before. [It means:] 'removed by conceptual construction' or 'removed from conceptual construction' — [both yield] <s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>. 'That which' (<s>yat</s>) indicates its essential nature. And such a [cognition] with respect to an object is also [cognition of] the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>). He says: cognition is awareness (<s>saṃvedana</s>). And that can also be without an object; therefore he says: 'with respect to an object' (<s>arthe</s>), i.e., with respect to a content. And that [object] is twofold, due to the distinction between particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) and universal (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>). Therefore he says: the meaning is 'with respect to the particular, i.e., form and the like.' Here, what was stated as '<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>' — he explains it by stating its essential nature: 'free from the conceptual construction of name, class, and the like.' That which is directed toward the sense-organ — that is <s>pratyakṣa</s>. Therein, name-construction is like '<s>Ḍittha</s>.' Class-construction is like 'cow.' By the word 'and the like' (<s>ādi</s>), quality, action, and substance are included. Therein, quality-construction is [like] 'white.' Action-construction is [like] 'cook.' Substance-construction is [like] 'staff-bearer.' Free from these constructions means: free from verbal [overlay] — because the particular alone is its cause. And it has been said: 'For words do not exist in the object, nor are they of its nature, such that when it appears, they too would appear' and so forth. 'That which is directed toward the sense-organ' and so on: by 'that' (<s>tat</s>), the previously indicated [cognition] is referred to. '<s>Akṣas</s>' are the sense-organs.

body.text: tataścākṣamakṣaṃ pratīndriyamindriyaṃ prativartata iti pratyakṣam / āha / yathendriyasāmarthyājjñānamutpadyate tathā viṣayasāmarthyādapi tatkasmādindriyeṇaiva vyapadeśo na viṣayeṇeti? / atrocyate / asādhāraṇatvādindriyasya sādharaṇatvāccārthasyeti / tathā hi / indriyamindriyavijñānasyaiva heturityasādharaṇam / arthastu manovijñānasyāpīti sādhāraṇaḥ / asādhāraṇena ca loke vyapadeśapravṛttiryathā bherīśabdo yavāṅkura iti / uktaṃ ca bhadantena /
body.translated_text: Therefore, that which is 'directed toward' (<s>prati</s>) the sense-organ, i.e., which operates toward each sense-organ respectively — that is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception). He asks: Just as cognition arises from the capacity of the sense-organ, so it also [arises] from the capacity of the object — so why is the designation made by the sense-organ alone and not by the object? To this it is said: because the sense-organ is uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>), while the object is common (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>). For indeed, the sense-organ is a cause only of sense-organ consciousness — hence it is uncommon. But the object is [a cause] also of mental consciousness — hence it is common. And in the world, designation proceeds by the uncommon [factor], as in 'the sound of a drum' or 'a barley-sprout.' And the venerable elder (<s>Bhadanta</s>) has said:

body.text: asādhāraṇahetutvādakṣaistadyapariśyate ityādi / āha / manovijñānādyapi pratyakṣamityuktaṃ na ca tadanena saṃgṛhītamiti kathaṃ vyāpitā lakṣaṇasya / ucyate / kalpanāpoḍhaṃ yattajjñānarthe rūpādau ityanenārthasākṣātkāritvagrahaṇānmanovijñānaderapi tadavyabhicārātsaṃgṛhītameva tanmānasam / laukikaṃ tu pratyakṣamadhikṛtyāvyayībhāvaḥ / iti kṛtaṃ prasaṅgeṇa / gamanikāmātrametat // anumānamityādi / anumitiramumānam / tacca liṅgādarthadarśanamāliṅgaṃ punastrirūpamuktam / pakṣadharmatvādi / tasmātrirūpālliṅgādyadanumeye 'rthe dharmaviśiṣṭe dharmiṇi jñānamutpadyate kiṃviśiṣṭam? agniratra dhūmāt anityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvāt tadanumānamiti / udāharaṇadvayaṃ tu vastusādhanakāryasvabhāvākhyahetudvayakhyāpanārtham / adhunā phalamāha / ubhayatretyādi / ubhatra pratyekṣe 'numāne ca / tadeva jñānaṃ pratyakṣanumānalakṣaṇam / phalaṃ kāryam / kutaḥ? / adhigamarūpatvāt / adhigamaḥ paricchedastadrūpatvāt / tathāhi paricchedarūpameva jñānamutpadyate / na ca paricchedādṛte anyajjñānaṃ phalam / bhinnādhikaraṇatvāt / ityatra bahu vaktavyam alaṃ prasaṅgena / sarvathā na pratyakṣānumānābhyāmanyadvibhinnaṃ phalamastīti / āha / yadyevaṃ pramāṇābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ / tabdhāvābhimatayoḥ pratyakṣānumānayoḥ phalatvāt / pramāṇābhāve ca tatphalasyāpyabhāvaḥ iti /
body.translated_text: 'Because of being an exclusive reason, it is not examined by the senses' and so on. [Objection:] He says — mental cognition (<s>manovijñāna</s>) and so on have also been said to be perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), yet these are not included by this [definition]; so how is the definition comprehensive? [Reply:] It is said — by the phrase 'that which is free from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>), that cognition regarding an object such as form and so on,' the grasping of direct acquaintance with the object is included; and since mental [perception] also does not deviate from that, it too is indeed included. The indeclinable compound, however, is used with reference to ordinary (<s>laukika</s>) perception. Enough of this digression; this is merely an indication. 'Inference' (<s>anumāna</s>) and so on — inferential cognition (<s>anumiti</s>) is inference. And that is the seeing of an object from a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>); the logical mark is said to have three characteristics (<s>trirūpa</s>) — being a property of the thesis (<s>pakṣadharmatva</s>) and so on. Therefore, from a logical mark possessing the three characteristics, when cognition arises regarding the object to be inferred — the property-bearer qualified by a property — what kind [of cognition is it]? 'There is fire here, from smoke'; 'Sound is non-eternal, because of being produced' — that is inference. The two examples are for making known the two types of reason called 'existence-proving' (<s>vastusādhana</s>) and 'nature-of-effect' (<s>kāryasvabhāva</s>). Now he states the result (<s>phala</s>): 'In both' and so on — 'in both' means in perception and in inference. That very cognition, characterized as perception or inference, is the result, i.e., the effect. Why? Because it has the nature of apprehension (<s>adhigama</s>). Apprehension is determination (<s>pariccheda</s>); because it has that nature. For indeed, cognition arises in the very form of determination. And apart from determination, there is no other cognition that is the result, because of being in different substrates. Here much could be said — enough of this digression. In all ways, there is no result separate and distinct from perception and inference. [Objection:] He says — if so, there would be the undesirable consequence of the absence of valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), since the accepted [means] — perception and inference — would themselves be the result (<s>phala</s>); and in the absence of a [distinct] valid means of knowledge, its result too would be absent.

body.text: tatra pramāṇābhāvanirācikīrṣayāha / savyāpāravatkhyāteḥ pramāṇatvamiti saha vyāpāreṇa viṣayagrahaṇalakṣaṇena vartate iti savyāpāram / pramāṇamiti gamyate / savyāpāramasyā vidyata iti savyāpāravatī / khyātiriti gamyate / savyāpāravatī cāsau khyātiśca savyāpāravatkhyātiḥ pratītiḥ / tasyāḥ savyāpāravattyāḥ khyāteḥ pramāṇatvamiti / etaduktaṃ bhavati / viṣayākāraṃ jñānamutpadyamānaṃ viṣayaṃ gṛṇhadevotpadyate iti pratīteḥ grāhakākārasya pramāṇateti / anye tu saṃścāsau vyāpāraḥ sadvyāpāraḥ pramāṇavyavasthākāritvātsannityucyate / so 'syā vidyata iti sadyāpāravatī śeṣaṃ pūrvavat vyācakṣate / ityukte pratyakṣānumāne // adhunā pratyekṣābhāsamāha / kalpanājñānamarthāntare pratyakṣābhāsam / etadeva grahaṇavākyaṃ vyācikhyāsurāha / yajjñānaṃ ghaṭaḥ paṭa iti vā vikalpayataḥ śabdāropitamutpadyate / arthāntare sāmānyalakṣaṇe / tadarthasvalakṣaṇāviṣayatvāt / sāmānyalakṣaṇaviṣayatvādityarthaḥ / uktaṃ pratyakṣābhāsam //
body.translated_text: In order to refute the absence of valid means of knowledge, he says: 'The status of being a valid means of knowledge belongs to cognition (<s>khyāti</s>) that possesses operation (<s>savyāpāravat</s>).' That which functions together with the operation characterized by grasping an object is called 'possessing operation' (<s>savyāpāra</s>), and is understood to be a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). That which possesses this operation is 'endowed with operation' (<s>savyāpāravatī</s>), and is understood to be cognition (<s>khyāti</s>). It is both endowed with operation and a cognition — hence 'cognition endowed with operation' (<s>savyāpāravatkhyāti</s>), i.e., awareness (<s>pratīti</s>). The status of being a valid means of knowledge belongs to that cognition endowed with operation. What this means is: cognition, arising in the form of the object, necessarily grasps the object as it arises — therefore the grasping aspect of awareness has the status of being a valid means of knowledge. Others, however, explain: 'that operation which is real' — 'real' is said because it effects the determination of the valid means of knowledge; 'that which possesses this [real operation]' is 'endowed with real operation' — the rest they explain as before. Thus perception and inference have been stated. Now he states the semblance of perception (<s>pratyakṣābhāsa</s>): 'Conceptual cognition (<s>kalpanājñāna</s>) regarding another object is a semblance of perception.' Wishing to explain this very statement of the definition, he says: that cognition which arises for one who conceptualizes 'this is a pot' or 'this is a cloth,' superimposed by words — regarding another object, [namely] the general characteristic (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>) — because it does not have the particular characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) of the object as its domain; the meaning is: because it has the general characteristic as its domain. Thus the semblance of perception has been stated.

body.text: sāṃpratamanumānābhāsamāha / hetvābhāsapūrvakaṃ hetvābhāsanimittaṃ jñānamanumānābhāsam / vyabhicārāt / etadeva vyācaṣṭe / hetvābhāso hi bahuprakāra uktaḥ asti vādibhedena / tasmāt hetvābhāsāt yadanumeye 'rthe dharmaviśiṣṭe dharmiṇi jñānam avyutpannasya asiddhādisvarūpānabhijñasya bhavati tadanumānābhāsam / ityuktaṃ pratyakṣādicatuṣṭayam // idānīmuktaśeṣaṃ duṣaṇamabhidhātukāma āha / sādhanadoṣodbhāvanāni dūṣaṇāni / pramāṇadoṣaprakaṭanānītyarthaḥ / bahuvacananirdeśaḥ pratyekamapi pratijñādidoṣāṇāṃ dūṣaṇatvāt / etānyeva daśayīrta / sādhanadoṣo nyūnatvam / sāmānyena viśeṣamāha / pakṣadoṣaḥ pratyakṣadiviruddhatvam / pratyakṣādiviruddhā pratijñetyevamādi / hetudoṣaḥ asiddhānaikāntikaviruddhatvam / asiddho heturityevamādi / evaṃ dṛṣṭāntadoṣāḥ sādhanadharmādyasiddhatvam / tasyodbhāvanamiti / tasya pratyakṣaviruddhahetvādeḥ prakāśanaṃ prāśnikapratyāyanaṃ na tudbhāvanamātrameva / dūṣaṇamiti sāmānyena dūṣaṇajātyanatikramādekavacanamiti / uktaṃ dūṣaṇam // adhunā dūṣāṇābhāsamāha / abhūtasādhanadoṣodbhāvanāni dūṣaṇābhāsāni / abhūtamavidyamānameva tadyataḥ sādhanadoṣaṃ sāmānyanodbhāvayanti prakāśayanti yāni tāni jātidūṣaṇābhāsāni / etadeva darśayati / saṃpūrṇe sādhane avayave nyūnatvavacanam / nyūnamidamityevaṃbhūtam / aduṣṭapakṣe pakṣa doṣavacanam ityādi nigadasiddham / yāvad etāni duṣaṇābhāsāni kim? / ityata āha / nahyebhiḥ parapakṣo dūṣyate / kutaḥ? / niravadyatvātparapakṣasya / ityuparamyate śāstrakaraṇāt //
body.translated_text: Now [the text] states what pseudo-inference (<s>anumānābhāsa</s>) is. Knowledge of the inferred object that is preceded by, i.e. caused by, a pseudo-reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) is pseudo-inference — because of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>). [The text itself] explains this: The pseudo-reason has been stated to be of many kinds, depending on the [type of] disputant. Therefore, the knowledge that arises in one who is uninstructed, i.e. unacquainted with the true nature of the unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>) etc., regarding the inferred object — the property-bearer qualified by the property — that is pseudo-inference. Thus the fourfold [set] beginning with perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) has been expounded. Now, wishing to state what remains to be said — namely, refutation (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>) — [the text] states: 'Refutations (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>) are the exposures of the faults of the proof (<s>sādhana</s>)' — meaning, the revelations of the faults of the means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>). The use of the plural indicates [that there are refutations] for each of the faults of the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>) and so forth individually.

body.text: śāstraparisamāptau tatsvarūpapratipādanāyaivāha / padārthamātramityādi / padārthamātramiti sādhanādipadoddeśamātrama / ākhyātaṃ kathitam / ādau prathamam / diṅmātrasiddhaye nyāyadiṅmātrasiddhayartham / yātra yuktiranvayavyatirekalakṣaṇā / ayuktirvā asiddhādibhedā / sānyatra pramāṇasamuccayādau / suvicāritā prapañcena nirūpitetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: At the completion of the <s>śāstra</s>, in order to indicate its [overall] character, [the text] states: 'Only the bare categories' etc. 'Only the bare categories' means merely the enumeration of the terms 'proof' (<s>sādhana</s>) and so forth. 'Has been explained' means stated. 'At first' means initially. 'For the purpose of establishing a mere indication of the logical method' — i.e., for the purpose of establishing merely the direction of logic. The reasoning characterized by positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) and negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>), or the absence of reasoning characterized by the varieties of the unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>) etc. — that is 'examined in detail elsewhere,' i.e. investigated at length in the <s>Pramāṇasamuccaya</s> and other [works]; that is the meaning.

children.translated_text: Whatever merit has been obtained here by me through expounding the <s>Nyāyapraveśaka</s> —
may beings, through that [merit], obtain the pleasure of entering into logic and the other [sciences]!

body.text: samāptā ceyaṃ śiṣyahitā nāma nyāyapraveśakaṭīkā //
body.translated_text: And this commentary on the <s>Nyāyapraveśa</s>, named <s>Śiṣyahitā</s> (Beneficial to Students), is completed.

body.text: kṛtiriyaṃ haribhadrasūreḥ //
body.translated_text: This is the work of <s>Haribhadrasūri</s>.
